# Use Case Lab — Full Corpus

A working atlas of where Ethereum meets the real world. Each entry below is one application of Ethereum to a specific real-world problem, with the cypherpunk reason a centralized version would fail.

Site: https://usecaselab.org
Source: https://github.com/usecaselab/explorer

---

# Personas (18)

## Civic Participant

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/civic-participant

### Example people

- Hassan, Civil engineer, Amman
- Aiko, Ward resident, Osaka
- Rosa, Procurement committee member, Mexico City

### Desires

1. I want to see where my tax money actually went
   Public budgets are executed in spreadsheets nobody sees and summarized in reports a year out of date, so government payments executed onchain, with each transfer traceable from appropriation to vendor, let anyone follow spending in real time.
   Related ideas: budget-execution-tracking, community-space-allocation

2. I want to know why my permit was denied and who decided
   When a zoning appeal, a benefits claim, or a contract award goes against me, I get a one-line outcome and no record of who weighed what. A tamper-evident log of which official, which rule, and which inputs produced the decision would let me actually contest it.
   Related ideas: ai-adjudicators, beneficial-ownership, construction-permits-housing, futarchy-public-policy, participatory-budgeting, public-procurement-lifecycle

3. I want my civil records under my own control, not stuck in the office that issued them
   Birth, marriage, and death records govern every official interaction yet sit in physical files that can be lost or held hostage to a fee, so civil registries that issue them as signed onchain attestations let a citizen hold their proof.
   Related ideas: civil-registry-records, firearm-licensing-registration

4. I want environmental and housing rules enforced when they're broken, not years later
   Environmental thresholds and housing covenants are rules whose enforcement lags so far behind violations that the harm is done first, so continuous measurement piped to onchain rule engines records a violation the same hour a threshold is crossed.
   Related ideas: affordable-housing-covenants, city-climate-commitment-tracking, environmental-measurement-and-verification, environmental-threshold-enforcement

---

## Community Organizer

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/community-organizer

### Example people

- Naledi, Tenants' association leader, Cape Town
- Marcus, Neighborhood council chair, Detroit
- Lena, Housing cooperative coordinator, Berlin

### Desires

1. I want a local currency for my neighborhood that doesn't die when the operator quits
   We've tried timebanks and local scrip and every one of them folded when the person running the spreadsheet moved on or the platform shut down. I want issuance rules, balances, and redemption to live somewhere the community keeps running even when I step back.
   Related ideas: community-currencies, cooperative-and-local-marketplaces, peer-to-peer-energy-markets

2. I want to pool capital with my neighbors without paying a bank to do it
   Lending circles and mutual-aid pools cost money to administer through banks and hold more cash than they need, so onchain lending pools set contribution and disbursement rules in code and return the savings to members instead of a custodian.
   Related ideas: cooperative-lending-pools

3. I want my block to finance its own solar roof or fiber line and pay investors back from what it earns
   Our co-op solar project is too small for a bank and too structured for a GoFundMe, so it just doesn't happen. I want a way to take small investments from neighbors and outside backers and pay them back from the meter revenue, with the repayment schedule something they can verify rather than trust me on.
   Related ideas: land-trust-housing-coop-coordination, local-infrastructure-bonds, renewable-project-financing

4. I want to watch the money my neighborhood voted on actually move
   Participatory-budgeting votes disappear into a general-fund line item the community cannot track, so budget allocations executed through onchain payments, with each transfer traceable to the project it was meant to fund, close the gap between the vote and the spending.
   Related ideas: community-space-allocation, participatory-budgeting

5. I want the affordable-housing and climate commitments my city signed to actually hold
   Cities quietly fall out of compliance with their housing covenants and emissions targets because enforcement is starved and the data is unqueryable, so onchain registries fed by attested rent rolls and emissions data make non-compliance visible the moment it happens.
   Related ideas: affordable-housing-covenants, city-climate-commitment-tracking

6. I want a rent strike or buyer's pledge that only triggers once enough neighbors are in
   Every rent strike I've tried to organize dies in the "I'll do it if everyone else does" phase. I want people to be able to commit publicly with their pledge held in escrow, so the action goes live the moment we cross the threshold and nobody is exposed alone.
   Related ideas: hyperstition-markets

---

## Creator

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/creator

### Example people

- Maya, Podcaster, São Paulo
- Joon, Electronic musician, Seoul
- Sarah, Fiction writer, Manchester

### Desires

1. I want to keep more of what I sell
   Platforms take 10 to 30 percent of every sale and hold the money for weeks, so settling payments onchain with smart contracts that split revenue at the moment of sale lets a creator keep the cut and skip the wait.
   Related ideas: creator-storefronts, film-tv-residuals, music-sync-licensing, pay-per-use-micropayments

2. I want to prove I made what I made
   Government IP registries are slow and per-jurisdiction while platform timestamps can be rewritten, so a signed onchain commitment made the moment of creation gives a creator evidence of origin that anyone can verify without trusting the hosting platform.
   Related ideas: content-authenticity-proofs, ip-registration-prior-art

3. I want to keep reaching my followers if a platform suspends me
   When my account gets locked or a platform decides my niche is off-brand, the audience I spent years building disappears overnight. If my follower list lived on a portable onchain graph instead of inside the app, I could message and sell to those same people from somewhere else the next day.
   Related ideas: portable-social-identity

4. I want my earliest backers to get paid back when something I make takes off
   The hundred people who funded my first record get a tote bag and a thank-you, even when the record ends up paying my rent for three years. If I could issue them a small revenue share that pays out automatically from streaming income, the people who took the risk would actually share in the reward.
   Related ideas: fan-funded-media, ip-assets

5. I want to trust the view and revenue numbers the platform pays me on
   My royalty statement says I had 412,000 streams last quarter and I have no way to check whether that's the real number or the number after the platform's accounting. If plays and ad views were counted against a log I could audit, I'd know my paycheck matched the activity instead of taking the platform's word for it.
   Related ideas: ad-influencer-metrics, referral-affiliate-payouts

6. I want compensation when AI is trained on my work
   Foundation models are trained on creators' work without notice on datasets that are rarely disclosed, so onchain provenance for training data lets a creator see if their work is included, license it, and be paid when those models earn.
   Related ideas: ai-model-data-markets

7. I want my income not to vanish overnight when an algorithm decides my topic is off-brand
   Platforms can demonetize a video, shadow-ban a hashtag, or quietly throttle my reach for any reason their policy team chooses, and the only appeal is a form that disappears into a queue. Revenue-eligible publishing on rails the platform can't unilaterally switch off means my paycheck depends on the work, not on whether my topic is on-brand this quarter.
   Related ideas: curation-markets

---

## Donor

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/donor

### Example people

- Helen, Disaster-relief donor, Toronto
- Idris, Foundation administrator, Dubai
- Sofia, Scholarship director, Buenos Aires

### Desires

1. I want to see where my money actually went
   Donations are pooled and regranted through accounting the donor never sees, severing the link between a gift and a household, so settling transfers onchain with every hop visible lets a donor follow a contribution from gift to recipient.
   Related ideas: direct-cash-transfer-programs, fund-flows-disaster-relief

2. I want to pay for delivered outcomes, not for promises
   Grants are paid upfront against proposed outcomes and reported on by the same organization seeking the next grant, so conditioning payments on independently verified milestones attested onchain aligns funding with what programs achieve rather than how they tell the story.
   Related ideas: impact-certificates, milestone-scholarship-disbursement, outcome-based-funding

3. I want the people a program serves to have a say in how the money is spent
   Budgets are decided by program officers in another city who have never met the families a program serves, and the people closest to the need have no vote in how a dollar gets split. Letting recipients allocate funds directly, with every transfer traceable back to the decision behind it, puts the call in the hands of the people living the problem.
   Related ideas: participatory-budgeting

---

## Fan

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/fan

### Example people

- Yuki, Indie music fan, Tokyo
- Tomas, Documentary backer, Mexico City
- Wei, MMO player, Shenzhen

### Desires

1. I want a real stake in the artists and projects I back early
   Tip jars, merchandise, and pre-sold crowdfunding rewards never let a fan share in the upside their early support helped create, so onchain instruments make it practical to issue fractional revenue shares that pay out automatically when the project earns.
   Related ideas: fan-funded-media, opportunity-markets

2. I want the money I spend on a ticket to reach the artist
   Concert tickets reappear on resale platforms at multiples of face value with the markup going to scalpers, so tickets issued as onchain assets with resale rights in the contract let the artist cap secondary prices and collect a resale share.
   Related ideas: event-ticket-resale

3. I want to actually own the items and time I sank into a game
   In-game items and progress sit on a studio's servers under terms that let the operator freeze accounts or shut the game down, but holding them as onchain assets keeps ownership with the player and lets the items move to any marketplace.
   Related ideas: player-owned-in-game-assets

4. I want to be paid when the mods and content I make drive the game
   Mods and user-generated content keep players engaged long past a game's launch, yet platforms rarely pay the modders, so onchain royalty contracts can route a share of the downstream activity to creators using the usage data the platform already collects.
   Related ideas: ugc-mod-royalties

---

## Farmer

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/farmer

### Example people

- Joseph, Maize and bean farmer, Eldoret
- Elena, Vineyard grower, Mendoza
- Tomás, Coffee cooperative lead, Antigua

### Desires

1. I want subsidy and insurance payments to arrive when the loss happens, not months later
   Agricultural subsidies and weather insurance routinely arrive months after the gap they exist to cover has swallowed the season, so smart contracts triggered by satellite rainfall data or government attestations release funds onchain the day a threshold is crossed.
   Related ideas: agricultural-subsidy-disbursement, parametric-weather-insurance

2. I want to borrow against my land and my standing crop without paying 80 percent interest
   Smallholders are invisible to banks because pre-harvest credit has no collateral and their land carries no recognized title, so tokenized future-crop receipts and onchain land titles give a lender collateral it can price and repaid automatically at harvest sale.
   Related ideas: harvest-pre-financing, informal-land-tenure-formalization

3. I want to get paid for the cover crops and hedgerows I plant, not just the bushels I sell
   Buyers price my maize by weight and ignore the soil work that took years, while carbon programs gate payouts behind audits that cost more than a smallholder will ever earn from them. Satellite measurement plus onchain payouts would let me earn for the carbon and habitat my practices build without an auditor pocketing the margin.
   Related ideas: regenerative-practice-incentives

4. I want premium buyers to verify our quality without $10,000 in certification fees
   Specialty buyers pay more for verified origin, but paper certification costs fall hardest on the small producers most likely to meet the standard, so onchain provenance for each lot lets a cooperative document quality cheaply and keep the premium.
   Related ideas: small-producer-sourcing

5. I want water use measured so the neighbors with deeper wells stop draining the aquifer
   In drought-prone regions overuse is profitable and undetectable under self-reported metering until the aquifer is gone, so onchain water-rights markets with continuous metering make overuse visible per well and let a farmer sell unused rights to a neighbor.
   Related ideas: water-rights-markets

---

## Founder

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/founder

### Example people

- Anya, Technical cofounder, Berlin
- Femi, Serial entrepreneur, Lagos
- Mia, Healthtech founder, Toronto

### Desires

1. I want to pay and be paid across borders without three-day waits and percent-of-payroll fees
   A distributed team means moving money to ten countries the same day, where wire fees, FX spreads, and late-transfer guesswork add up, so stablecoin payroll settled onchain delivers funds in minutes and generates the per-payee records tax authorities want.
   Related ideas: cross-border-payroll

2. I want a cap table everyone can read from the same source
   Cap tables live on vendor platforms that charge by the seat and reconcile poorly with equity portals and investor records, so a cap table represented onchain, with each issuance signed by its parties, gives everyone the same authoritative view.
   Related ideas: cap-tables

3. I want to spend my first months building, not refiling the same documents
   Forming a company takes weeks across several agencies and then every bank and customer asks for the same incorporation packet again, so onchain business registries let a founder present verifiable attestations issued by the registry instead of repeating the proof.
   Related ideas: business-formation-licensing

4. I want partnership payouts to fire on the numbers, not on a partner's word
   When a partner owes me a revenue share or a milestone payment, they own the dashboard that decides what I'm owed and I either trust their export or chase them for months. A contract that pays out against a billing feed both sides signed off on upfront takes the discretion away from whichever side holds the books.
   Related ideas: earnouts-contingent-payments

---

## Freelance Professional

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/freelance-professional

### Example people

- Camille, UX consultant, Montreal
- Tomás, Backend engineer, Buenos Aires
- Hana, Architect, Berlin

### Desires

1. I want to pay and get paid across borders without losing a tenth of every job
   A freelancer working across borders loses real money to wire fees, FX spreads, and platforms that hold funds for a week, so settling invoices onchain in stablecoins collapses the chain of intermediaries into a single transaction that arrives in minutes.
   Related ideas: cross-border-payroll

2. I want to turn a net-60 invoice into rent money this week
   Half my clients pay on net-60 or net-90 and I'm fronting rent from savings while a signed invoice sits in someone's AP queue. Factoring exists for big firms with big invoices; I want a pool that will advance against my invoice the day I send it, priced off my actual track record.
   Related ideas: invoice-receivables-financing

3. I want my contracts to be enforceable without hiring a lawyer
   When a client refuses to pay, a freelancer can only write off the invoice or sue across jurisdictions, so smart contracts holding the fee in escrow until a milestone is met, with disputes routed to onchain arbitration, make enforcement affordable.
   Related ideas: dispute-resolution

4. I want my credentials and ratings to travel with me
   A freelancer who moves between platforms or countries loses the reviews and credentials locked in databases the platform owns, so attestations of credentials and completed engagements, committed onchain by the issuer or client, let them carry their record anywhere.
   Related ideas: portable-professional-credentials

---

## Gig Worker

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/gig-worker

### Example people

- Marcus, Rideshare driver, Atlanta
- Renata, Food-delivery courier, Lisbon
- Dele, Truck owner-operator, Lagos

### Desires

1. I want to be paid the moment the work is done
   A driver or contractor often waits a week or more for pay because the platform reconciles on its own cycle, but smart contracts that release funds the moment a delivery is signed for, against signals already collected, close the gap to minutes.
   Related ideas: delivery-triggered-payments

2. I want my ratings and history to travel with me
   A worker's ratings and job history are an asset built over thousands of hours yet trapped in a platform's database, so signed onchain attestations of completed jobs and ratings, issued by the platform but owned by the worker, let that reputation travel anywhere.
   Related ideas: portable-ratings-reviews, spot-freight-trucking

3. I want lenders to see the income I actually earn
   Banks underwrite against W-2s and tax returns, so a gig worker with steady income across three platforms reads as irregular deposits and gets declined, but verifiable onchain payment histories from the platforms they use give a lender something concrete to underwrite.
   Related ideas: credit-scoring

---

## Homeowner

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/homeowner

### Example people

- Linda, Mortgage holder, Phoenix
- Diego, First-time buyer, Lisbon
- Hannah, Housing co-op board member, Brooklyn

### Desires

1. I want to see who holds my mortgage and how my payments are applied
   After a mortgage is resold the borrower rarely knows who holds the note or whether the servicer's escrow math is right, but a mortgage held onchain, with every payment, rate adjustment, and assignment committed in the open, lets the borrower verify the figures.
   Related ideas: mortgage-home-equity-rails

2. I want to close on a house in a week instead of paying a title company to spend two months chasing paper
   Every closing means a title company billing me to retrace a chain of deeds that already exists in a county office, and a missed signature can push the date out twice. If the title lived onchain and the deed transferred when escrow released, the search and the wait both disappear without changing what's legally true.
   Related ideas: title-escrow, wills-estate-execution

---

## Investor

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/investor

### Example people

- Tomás, Retail investor, Lisbon
- Priya, Wealth advisor, Mumbai
- Akosua, Family office principal, Accra

### Desires

1. I want to buy government bonds and reinsurance the way the big funds do, not through a broker that marks them up
   A 10-year treasury or a slice of a reinsurance pool is something pension funds buy at par, but to get there as a retail investor I go through a broker who sets a $50k minimum and adds a spread. Issuing these instruments onchain lets me buy a $500 piece at the same price the desk pays.
   Related ideas: local-infrastructure-bonds, reinsurance, renewable-project-financing, revenue-bonds, sovereign-municipal-bonds

2. I want to know the carbon credits and green bonds I bought are actually doing what the brochure said
   The carbon offsets and renewable-yield products in my portfolio come with PDFs from the issuer and a registry that the same issuer pays into, and I have no way to check whether the underlying project is still running. Sensor data and project performance posted onchain as it happens lets me audit my own holdings instead of trusting the brochure.
   Related ideas: carbon-biodiversity-credits, environmental-measurement-and-verification

3. I want my kids to inherit my portfolio without a year of probate and a lawyer's cut
   My brokerage, pension, and insurance accounts each have their own beneficiary forms, surrender procedures, and lawyers, and when my father died it took a year to move anything. Assets held onchain with succession encoded in a smart contract pass to my heirs the moment the conditions are met, without an estate intermediary.
   Related ideas: tokenized-policies-for-resale, wills-estate-execution

---

## Journalist

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/journalist

### Example people

- Layla, Investigative journalist, Beirut
- Marcus, Protest videographer, Atlanta
- Anna, Freelance journalist, Warsaw

### Desires

1. I want to prove a piece of footage or evidence is genuinely mine
   Reporters are routinely accused of staging or doctoring their material, so a signed onchain commitment made the moment a photo or video is captured gives verifiable proof of authorship and time that any reader or court can independently check.
   Related ideas: content-authenticity-proofs

2. I want a source to be able to send me documents without leaving a trail my government can subpoena
   SecureDrop sits on servers somebody owns and can be ordered to hand over logs, and any file I receive carries metadata that can burn the sender. I want a drop where the source proves they're a real insider without revealing who, and where no central operator holds records that can be compelled.
   Related ideas: journalist-source-protection, whistleblower-evidence-integrity

3. I want my reporting record to travel with me when I move outlets
   A journalist's bylines, awards, and employment history are trapped in the systems of past outlets, so portable credentials anchored onchain and issued by editors and former employers let them present a verifiable record independent of any one outlet.
   Related ideas: portable-professional-credentials

---

## Manufacturer

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/manufacturer

### Example people

- Amara, Small-batch coffee roaster, Addis Ababa
- Wei, Contract electronics manufacturer, Shenzhen
- Ingrid, Plant operations director, Stuttgart

### Desires

1. I want buyers to tell my product apart from the knock-offs that copy my label
   Counterfeiters slap my brand on inferior parts and undercut me, and buyers cannot tell the difference until something fails. A component and assembly history recorded onchain at each step lets a buyer scan and confirm the unit in their hand is one I actually built.
   Related ideas: digital-product-passports, food-provenance-and-traceability, pharmaceutical-traceability

2. I want quality records that buyers and auditors can trust
   Batch and quality records sit in databases the manufacturer can edit, so recalls drag and auditors re-verify by hand, but records committed onchain as they are created give buyers, auditors, and regulators a quality history that cannot be quietly revised after the fact.
   Related ideas: manufacturing-batch-records

3. I want to reach buyers without losing my margin to middlemen
   Distributors and certification bodies own the buyer relationship and price a producer's access to it, but onchain sourcing records and direct settlement let a producer carry its own verifiable quality story to buyers and capture the margin that currently goes to the intermediary.
   Related ideas: small-producer-sourcing

4. I want to ship and get paid across borders without weeks of bank paperwork
   Cross-border shipping still runs on paper, where letters of credit take a week and bills of lading are couriered as physical originals, but issued onchain and settled against attested delivery data, the same documents release payment and goods in hours.
   Related ideas: customs-records, electronic-bill-of-lading, letters-of-credit

5. I want to finance production against the inventory I already hold
   A manufacturer struggles to borrow against finished goods because lenders cannot verify the inventory exists, is the quality claimed, and is unpledged, but inventory verified and recorded onchain, with each pledge registered, lets them borrow at a rate reflecting the real risk.
   Related ideas: inventory-verification-lending

6. I want my purchase orders to match my supplier's books without a month-end reconciliation
   My team and my supplier's team keep separate copies of every PO, invoice, and delivery note in unrelated ERP systems, and someone burns a week each month chasing down the mismatches. A purchase order both sides sign onto a shared onchain record means there is only one version to reconcile against.
   Related ideas: procurement

---

## Merchant

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/merchant

### Example people

- Halima, Electronics importer, Mombasa
- Diego, Mezcal cooperative lead, Oaxaca
- Priya, Shopkeeper, Birmingham

### Desires

1. I want to pay my overseas suppliers without losing a week and 4% to the banks
   When I wire $20,000 to a supplier, my bank takes a cut, the correspondent bank takes another, and the money lands four days later at a worse rate than I was quoted. Settling in stablecoins onchain lets the funds arrive same-day at the rate I actually see.
   Related ideas: customs-records, electronic-bill-of-lading, letters-of-credit

2. I want to keep my customer list and reviews when I leave a marketplace
   Amazon and Etsy hold my buyer emails and the years of reviews I built up, so the day I try to sell direct or switch platforms I start from zero. A portable onchain reputation and buyer identity travels with me when I move.
   Related ideas: cooperative-and-local-marketplaces, physical-goods-marketplaces

3. I want my origin claims to be checkable without paying a certifier every year
   Buyers pay a premium for single-origin or fair-trade goods, but the certification bodies charge fees a cooperative my size cannot afford and own the stamp that grants market access. Provenance recorded onchain at harvest, with inspectors signing their checks publicly, gives buyers the same confidence without the gatekeeper.
   Related ideas: small-producer-sourcing

4. I want to onboard to a new bank or marketplace without handing over my passport again
   Every bank, payment processor, and B2B marketplace makes me upload the same passport scan, company papers, and sanctions screening, and each one becomes a future data breach. A reusable proof that I have already been screened lets me onboard without re-submitting the documents.
   Related ideas: kyc-sanctions-proofs

---

## OSS Maintainer

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/oss-maintainer

### Example people

- Lukas, Library maintainer, Vienna
- Adaeze, Open-source contributor, Lagos
- Felipe, Build tool author, Porto Alegre

### Desires

1. I want the companies that depend on my library to actually pay for it
   Fortune 500 services import my package millions of times a month and the tip jar still has $40 in it, because there's no point in the build chain where commercial use triggers payment. If a license could meter commercial usage and route a small fee back through the dependency graph, the companies shipping my code in production would pay automatically instead of when someone remembers to.
   Related ideas: commercial-use-licensing, dependency-graph-funding, open-source-contribution-funding

## Patient

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/patient

### Example people

- Diane, Autoimmune patient, Cleveland
- Kwame, Parent and caregiver, Accra
- Yuki, Diabetes patient, Osaka

### Desires

1. I want my medical records under my own control
   A patient rebuilds their history from memory at every appointment because each provider's records sit in a separate system, so health records in patient-controlled storage with onchain access permissions let them grant and revoke provider access in seconds.
   Related ideas: patient-controlled-health-records, wearables-and-health-data-exchanges

2. I want insurance payouts when the trigger is met, not when an adjuster decides
   Patients pay premiums for years and then wait weeks while an adjuster decides whether an admission qualified, so parametric insurance contracts settled onchain against verifiable triggers like admission records and diagnostic codes pay out the moment the condition is met.
   Related ideas: parametric-health-insurance

3. I want to see and challenge the algorithm that decided my case
   Denials and prior authorization decisions run through models the insurer will not disclose, so adjudication models with weights and decision logs committed onchain let a patient see which model judged them and challenge it through neutral arbitration.
   Related ideas: ai-adjudicators, insurance-claims-adjudication

4. I want to verify the drugs and treatments I am taking are real
   Counterfeit medications kill hundreds of thousands a year and a patient cannot tell a real pack from a fake, so onchain provenance with each supply-chain handoff signed lets a pharmacist scan a pack and verify a legitimate manufacturer in seconds.
   Related ideas: pharmaceutical-traceability

5. I want to know the drug my doctor prescribed was tested honestly
   The trial that got my medication approved is summarized in a leaflet written by the company that sold it, and I have no way to tell whether bad outcomes were quietly dropped before publication. Trial protocols and raw readings committed at capture, where nobody can revise the record after the fact, would let an independent doctor tell me whether the evidence actually holds up.
   Related ideas: decentralized-clinical-trials, pre-registration-and-results

---

## Researcher

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/researcher

### Example people

- Aditi, Computational biologist, Bangalore
- Mateusz, Materials science postdoc, Warsaw
- Esther, Clinical trial lead, Nairobi

### Desires

1. I want to prove when I made this work, and that I made it first
   Priority disputes turn on dates researchers establish through slow, per-jurisdiction preprint timestamps, so a finding committed onchain at discovery with a cryptographic hash of the data gives evidence of priority any peer or funder can verify without trusting a platform.
   Related ideas: ip-registration-prior-art

2. I want credit when other people's papers are built on my dataset
   My dataset has been reused in forty papers and I am thanked in a footnote when I am thanked at all, while the lab that ran the followups gets the citation and the next grant. A signed record of who produced a dataset and which papers drew on it, with citation and payment routed back automatically, would make reuse visible and pay the people whose work the field is standing on.
   Related ideas: dataset-provenance-reuse-tracking, peer-review-markets

3. I want compensation when AI is trained on my work
   Foundation models are trained on published research without the producers' consent, so onchain provenance for training data lets a researcher see whether their papers are included, license their use, and receive payment when the resulting models generate revenue.
   Related ideas: ai-model-data-markets

4. I want trial and source data nobody can quietly rewrite
   Clinical trials and replication efforts depend on source data in a single sponsor-controlled database anyone could edit before publication, so source readings committed onchain at capture, with append-only updates, let everyone verify the data matches what was collected.
   Related ideas: decentralized-clinical-trials, pre-registration-and-results

5. I want to raise money against my own research without signing it away
   My university's tech transfer office takes a year to even read the disclosure, then asks for the majority of any upside in exchange for filing a patent I am not allowed to license myself. Letting me sell rights or revenue shares in my own work directly to backers, with the splits enforced automatically, would let me fund the next stage without surrendering the work.
   Related ideas: ip-assets

6. I want to know which papers will actually hold up before I build on them
   I have spent months chasing a result that the lab next door quietly failed to reproduce and never published. A market where researchers stake on whether a finding will replicate, settled against a pre-registered test, would surface what the field privately doubts long before a formal replication study lands.
   Related ideas: scientific-claim-markets, scientific-knowledge-graph

---

## Shopper

URL: https://usecaselab.org/persona/shopper

### Example people

- Eleni, Grocery shopper, Athens
- Devon, EV driver, Toronto
- Lakshmi, Apartment renter, Mumbai

### Desires

1. I want to know if the "free-range" carton actually came from a farm that lets the hens outside
   I pay double for ethical labels and have no way to tell whether the certifier ever visited the farm or whether the carton was relabeled in the warehouse. If each handoff from coop to shelf was signed onchain I could scan the carton and see the actual farm and the last inspection date.
   Related ideas: digital-product-passports, digital-vehicle-passports, food-provenance-and-traceability, pharmaceutical-traceability

2. I want to prove I'm over 18 to a website without uploading my passport to it
   Every age-gated site and every account signup wants a photo of my ID sitting on some vendor's server waiting to leak. A zero-knowledge proof tied to a credential my government already issued would let the site see "yes, over 18" and nothing else.
   Related ideas: age-eligibility-proofs, kyc-sanctions-proofs

3. I want to sell my old bike to a stranger without giving eBay 13 percent for holding the money
   The only reason I use a marketplace for a one-off sale is that neither side trusts the other to ship or pay first, and the platform charges a double-digit cut for that single service. Onchain escrow that releases when the buyer confirms delivery, plus a reputation I can carry between sites, would do the same job for cents.
   Related ideas: physical-goods-marketplaces, portable-ratings-reviews

4. I want to plug my EV into any charger and have it just bill me, without signing up for that network
   Every charging network wants its own app, account, and minimum top-up, because card fees make a single $4 session uneconomic to bill directly. Onchain micropayments that settle in fractions of a cent would let the car pay the charger per kilowatt-hour with no account in the middle.
   Related ideas: ev-charging-coordination, home-energy-grid-flexibility, pay-per-use-micropayments, peer-to-peer-energy-markets

5. I want my rental deposit back automatically when I move out clean, not whenever the landlord feels like it
   My landlord holds two months of rent in an account I cannot see and decides on his own timeline whether to return it, and the small-claims path costs more than the deposit. If the deposit sat in onchain escrow that released on a signed move-out inspection, the discretion goes away.
   Related ideas: insurance-claims-adjudication, mortgage-home-equity-rails, residential-leasing, title-escrow, tokenized-policies-for-resale, tradable-loyalty-points

# Ideas (107)

## Ad delivery and influencer metrics

ID: `ad-influencer-metrics`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ad-influencer-metrics

### Problem

Ad networks report impressions and clicks using their own unauditable metrics, enabling widespread fraud. Brands also pay influencers based on self-reported or platform-reported reach and engagement that is trivially inflated through bots and fake followers.

### Solution

Transparent impression tracking and verifiable reach metrics — with optional zero-knowledge proofs for audience size — so advertisers can independently confirm that spend reached real human audiences.

### Why Ethereum

Ad fraud persists because the ad network reports on its own delivery, and any auditor it hires can be acquired or pressured by the platform it is supposed to check. Recording delivery onchain that no participant controls gives advertisers a measurement they can verify independently and prevents the network from revising the numbers afterward.

---

## Affordable housing covenant enforcement

ID: `affordable-housing-covenants`
Domains: Real Estate & Housing, Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/affordable-housing-covenants

### Problem

Affordable housing deed restrictions — requiring units to remain below market rate for 30, 50, or 99 years — are written into paper legal documents that must be manually checked at every ownership transfer, and routinely slip through conveyancing processes, effectively converting affordable units to market rate with no enforcement mechanism.

### Solution

Affordability restrictions encoded directly into property tokens that enforce covenants automatically at the point of transfer or rental — making it structurally impossible to sell or rent above the allowed price without the covenant being triggered.

### Why Ethereum

When a covenant lives only in paper records, enforcement depends on whichever office happens to review a transfer, and an owner with an incentive to convert the unit can count on the check being missed. Encoding the restriction into the asset onchain means the rule travels with the property and stays verifiable by tenants and the public rather than sitting with a registry that has to notice a violation.

---

## Age and eligibility proofs without identity disclosure

ID: `age-eligibility-proofs`
Domains: Identity
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/age-eligibility-proofs

### Problem

A teenager trying to prove they're 18 to access a website, or a doctor proving they hold a medical license to prescribe remotely, must hand over their full government ID — exposing date of birth, address, and ID number to a third party who only needed a yes/no answer — creating surveillance infrastructure and breach risk for a simple eligibility check.

### Solution

Zero-knowledge proofs that let individuals demonstrate they meet a threshold — over 18, licensed physician, accredited investor — without revealing the underlying document, name, or any other personal attribute beyond the specific claim being verified.

### Why Ethereum

A centralized verification service would see every site a person unlocks and would hold everyone's identity documents in one place that becomes a target for breaches. Building this with zero-knowledge proofs onchain lets a person prove a specific claim without revealing the underlying document, and keeps the check from being routed through a company that can log or leak it.

---

## Agricultural subsidy disbursement

ID: `agricultural-subsidy-disbursement`
Domains: Government, Food & Agriculture
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/agricultural-subsidy-disbursement

### Problem

Agricultural subsidy programs (e.g., EU Common Agricultural Policy direct payments, USDA conservation programs) require farmers to submit annual applications, undergo eligibility reviews, and wait months for payment — a process where administrative overhead consumes a significant share of program budgets and delays reach the farmers who need operating capital most. Eligibility conditions like acreage verification, crop compliance, and conservation practice adoption are checked manually by inspectors who can physically visit only a fraction of enrolled farms each year.

### Solution

Subsidy disbursements that execute automatically when satellite-verified acreage data, crop identification, and conservation practice adoption confirm eligibility — reducing administrative costs and getting payments to farmers at the start of the season rather than months after application.

### Why Ethereum

When subsidy payments depend on manual review, the agency controls the pace and the discretion, and farmers wait months while inspectors reach only a fraction of enrolled farms. Tying disbursement to verified eligibility data onchain makes the rule and the release visible to everyone, so payment timing follows the criteria rather than an administrator's queue or judgment.

---

## Provable AI adjudicators

ID: `ai-adjudicators`
Domains: AI
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ai-adjudicators

### Problem

AI is starting to make binding decisions: settling insurance claims, allocating grants, arbitrating disputes, moderating what stays up. When an AI reaches a verdict, the people affected have no way to confirm which model and inputs produced it. The operator can quietly swap in a cheaper or biased model, or deny that a decision was tampered with, and the party the decision went against has no recourse.

### Solution

AI adjudicators that carry a proof of how each verdict was reached, showing the disclosed model ran on the stated inputs. A claimant, applicant, or party to a dispute can check that the AI deciding their case is the one everyone agreed to, and that its decision was not swapped or edited after the fact.

### Why Ethereum

When the operator of an AI adjudicator is the only one who knows which model decided a case, the party it ruled against has to take the operator's word for it. Anchoring each verdict's proof onchain lets anyone check which model ran and on what inputs, so an AI making binding decisions answers to a record outside its operator's control.

---

## AI model and training data markets

ID: `ai-model-data-markets`
Domains: AI
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ai-model-data-markets

### Problem

AI models and training datasets are passed through ad-hoc channels with no enforceable licensing, usage metering, or royalty distribution — so creators lose control the moment they publish. The problem runs deeper for the creative workers whose output trained these models: writers, artists, and photographers have no mechanism to verify whether their work was included in a training corpus, no ability to opt out retroactively, and no way to claim revenue from models that directly replicate their style.

### Solution

Tokenized AI models and training datasets with programmable licensing terms set at registration — enabling usage metering, automatic royalty distribution to all rights holders, and cryptographic provenance records that let creators verify inclusion in training corpora and receive proportional compensation without relying on AI companies to voluntarily disclose what they trained on.

### Why Ethereum

If a marketplace ran on one company's platform, that operator would report usage on its own systems and decide what creators are owed, leaving the same disclosure gap that lets AI companies stay quiet about what they trained on. Putting licensing and provenance onchain keeps the usage record outside any operator's control, so creators can verify whether their work was used and claim compensation without depending on a platform to be honest.

---

## Business registries and beneficial ownership

ID: `beneficial-ownership`
Domains: Government, Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/beneficial-ownership

### Problem

Verifying a company's registration, licensing status, or true ownership requires navigating multiple disconnected databases — and existing beneficial ownership registries rely on self-reported filings with no verification mechanism, allowing shell company structures to hide the real owners of assets across jurisdictions. This structural opacity is systematically exploited for money laundering, sanctions evasion, and tax fraud.

### Solution

Cryptographically attested business registration and beneficial ownership records that chain legal entities to verified ultimate owners across jurisdictions — enabling instant verification for regulators, banks, and counterparties without relying on self-filed declarations or bilateral data-sharing between registries.

### Why Ethereum

Ownership registries today sit inside individual governments, so verification across borders depends on slow cooperation and a registry can be pressured to obscure who really controls an asset. A neutral onchain register lets banks, regulators, and counterparties check signed ownership attestations directly, without trusting any one jurisdiction to keep its records honest or to share them.

---

## Budget execution tracking

ID: `budget-execution-tracking`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/budget-execution-tracking

### Problem

Public funds flow through opaque, fragmented databases between appropriation and expenditure, making it nearly impossible for citizens or auditors to trace how tax revenue is actually spent.

### Solution

Real-time tracking of public funds from appropriation to expenditure

### Why Ethereum

When the government keeps its own spending records, the body being audited also controls the records, and it can present a partial picture or revise entries before anyone outside sees them. Recording appropriations and expenditures onchain puts the trail where citizens and auditors can follow it directly, without depending on the agency's cooperation to confirm where tax revenue went.

---

## Business formation and licensing

ID: `business-formation-licensing`
Domains: Government, Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/business-formation-licensing

### Problem

Starting a business in most jurisdictions means coordinating with four to six separate agencies: the secretary of state for the entity, the IRS for an EIN, the state revenue department for sales-tax registration, the local government for a business license, and often a regulator for industry-specific licensing. Each has its own form, its own processing window, and its own way of communicating status. A founder waits weeks for paperwork that any of the agencies could in principle confirm in seconds, and any later proof to a bank, payment processor, or platform that the entity exists in good standing means going back to each issuer for a new certificate.

### Solution

A coordinated workflow where each agency issues its piece (incorporation, EIN, license, sales-tax registration) as a verifiable credential the founder holds, with signoffs anchored against issuer signing keys onchain. The founder reuses the same credential bundle to open a bank account, sign up with a processor, or apply for a contract, and a counterparty checks each piece against the issuing agency directly without that agency needing to operate a real-time lookup service.

### Why Ethereum

When business credentials are scattered across agency portals and paper certificates, anyone who needs to verify a founder's standing depends on whichever agency happens to have a working API or a willing clerk. Issuing the credentials onchain against state and federal signing keys lets the founder present them anywhere, and a bank or counterparty checks the actual issuer's signature rather than a vendor's claim about what the agency says.

---

## Cap tables

ID: `cap-tables`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/cap-tables

### Problem

Startup cap tables live in expensive, siloed platforms like Carta where ownership records can fall out of sync, transfers require manual legal work, and founders have no real-time, verifiable source of truth.

### Solution

A startup's cap table kept as an onchain record from incorporation onward, with issuance, vesting, and transfers written to it as they happen. Founders, investors, and employees read the same source of truth directly, and a transfer updates the record rather than requiring separate legal work to reconcile the official version later.

### Why Ethereum

When a cap table lives on a vendor's platform, founders and investors depend on that company to keep the record accurate, grant access, and not change its terms or pricing, and the official version can quietly diverge from what shareholders believe they hold. Recording ownership onchain gives every party the same signed record, verifiable directly and not held hostage to one provider.

---

## Carbon and biodiversity credit markets

ID: `carbon-biodiversity-credits`
Domains: Environment, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/carbon-biodiversity-credits

### Problem

Carbon credits and biodiversity offsets are traded as undifferentiated commodities despite vast differences in methodology and verification rigor, allowing low-quality credits to crowd out legitimate ones. Forests, watersheds, and biodiversity also lack liquid market representations.

### Solution

Differentiated environmental asset classes with onchain provenance, methodology metadata, and verification quality — enabling transparent pricing of ecological assets and markets that reward genuine impact.

### Why Ethereum

Credit quality today depends on rating agencies and registries whose judgments are opaque and whose business depends on the issuers they assess, so buyers cannot independently tell a rigorous credit from a weak one. Attaching provenance and methodology to each credit onchain lets buyers check quality themselves and makes double-counting visible to anyone, not just the registry.

## City climate commitment tracking

ID: `city-climate-commitment-tracking`
Domains: Government, Environment
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/city-climate-commitment-tracking

### Problem

Coalitions like C40 Cities and the Global Covenant of Mayors have enrolled hundreds of cities in public emissions reduction pledges — but compliance tracking relies on self-reported data submitted to central secretariats, with no neutral mechanism for member cities or the public to verify whether commitments are being met or to detect when cities quietly abandon targets.

### Solution

An onchain record where city governments record verified emissions data, policy milestones, and adaptation measures — with attestations from IoT sensor networks, third-party auditors, and satellite monitoring — creating a publicly auditable record that any city, funder, or citizen can inspect.

### Why Ethereum

When a coalition secretariat holds the only record of who pledged what, member cities can quietly walk back targets and the body tracking compliance has its own reason to report progress favorably. Logging commitments and attested data onchain where no single member or secretariat controls lets any city, funder, or citizen check the record directly, and a city cannot rewrite its own history after the fact.

## Civil registry and vital records

ID: `civil-registry-records`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/civil-registry-records

### Problem

Birth, death, marriage, and residency records sit in siloed, often paper-based systems that vary by jurisdiction. Records are vulnerable to loss, hard to reconcile when someone moves or a local office changes hands, and a citizen usually cannot get a verifiable copy without going back to the issuing office.

### Solution

Civil registry records issued and maintained in an interoperable, verifiable format, so a birth or marriage record can be checked by any authorized party and carried across jurisdictions. The record survives the loss of a local office's files and does not have to be reissued from scratch each time it is needed.

### Why Ethereum

A civil registry held by one office or one vendor depends entirely on that operator to keep it intact, grant access, and stay in business, and records can be lost, altered, or made inaccessible when administrations change. Anchoring the registry onchain keeps each record verifiable independent of the office that issued it, so a citizen's vital records do not vanish with a server or a change in government.

---

## Commercial-use licensing for open source

ID: `commercial-use-licensing`
Domains: Business Operations, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/commercial-use-licensing

### Problem

A maintainer is fine with their library being free for individuals, students, and research, and would prefer commercial users that integrate it into paid products to pay a license fee. The current options are bad: keep the license fully permissive and watch a vendor charge six figures for a hosted version of the work, relicense to AGPL and accept a fight with every commercial user, or move to a source-available license and accept the cost of policing it. None of these scale to a single maintainer with a day job.

### Solution

A dual-licensing model where commercial use is gated by an onchain license token. The maintainer publishes the terms, commercial users acquire the token by paying a fee that flows directly to the project's address, and the build or runtime checks the presence of a valid license tied to the user's identity. Compliance is cheaper than litigation, the maintainer does not need a legal department, and individual or non-commercial use stays untouched.

### Why Ethereum

License enforcement at the scale of an indie maintainer fails because the cost of detecting non-compliance and the cost of pursuing it are both higher than the license fee. Issuing license tokens onchain, with a public price and a verifiable record of who holds one, shifts the work from enforcement to verification: any party in the supply chain can check whether a commercial deployment holds a current license, and the maintainer collects the fee without negotiating individually with each vendor.

---

## Community currencies

ID: `community-currencies`
Domains: Finance, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/community-currencies

### Problem

Local economies leak spending to global platforms and distant supply chains, and communities that want to circulate a local currency lack reliable infrastructure to issue, govern, and settle it at meaningful scale.

### Solution

Place- or network-specific currencies used by defined communities (cities, cooperatives, regions) to keep spending local, incentivize participation, and fund public goods rather than leaking value to external markets

### Why Ethereum

When a community currency runs on a vendor's platform, the provider can freeze balances or shut the system down, leaving the local economy dependent on decisions the community does not control. Building it onchain keeps the currency's rules and record with the community that governs them, where anyone can audit the system and it keeps working regardless of any single company.

## Community space revenue and allocation

ID: `community-space-allocation`
Domains: Government, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/community-space-allocation

### Problem

Revenue from commercial use of public spaces — parks, plazas, community halls — flows into general municipal budgets where residents can't see how much their neighborhood's spaces generated or how those funds were spent. Allocation decisions happen in opaque committee processes with no audit trail, and community groups that maintain or improve a space have no formal mechanism to influence how it's governed.

### Solution

A transparent treasury for each community space where commercial booking revenue is publicly tracked and spending decisions are made through participatory governance by verified local residents — creating a direct feedback loop between a space's economic activity and its neighborhood's investment priorities.

### Why Ethereum

When booking revenue flows into a general municipal budget, residents lose sight of what their neighborhood's spaces earned and how it was spent, and allocation happens in committee rooms with no record they can check. A treasury onchain makes every payment and disbursement publicly auditable, so the people who use and maintain a space can see and govern the money it generates.

## Construction permits for housing

ID: `construction-permits-housing`
Domains: Government, Real Estate & Housing
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/construction-permits-housing

### Problem

A residential construction project, whether it is adding units, building an accessory dwelling, or redeveloping a lot, passes through a sequence of agency signoffs (planning, zoning, building, fire, environmental, sometimes utilities) where each step can take weeks or months and the applicant has no real-time view of which desk the file currently sits on. The delays and discretion at each stage feed the housing-supply gap that drives affordability problems in many cities, and applicants without political access tend to wait longer or get steered through more requirements than connected developers.

### Solution

A permit case file recorded onchain from submission through final sign-off, with each agency review, inspection result, and decision rationale logged as it happens. The applicant sees where the permit sits in real time, the public can compare which projects move quickly and which stall, and deviations from the standard timeline or procedure surface against a shared baseline rather than hiding inside one office's filing system.

### Why Ethereum

When permit timelines and decisions live inside agency systems, the same officials whose discretion the public is meant to check also control the record of how that discretion was exercised, and an applicant or a journalist has no independent way to see where in the chain a project is stuck or why. Anchoring the case file onchain keeps the timeline and the signoffs auditable by anyone, so a city's commitment to predictable permitting becomes visible rather than something residents have to take on trust.

---

## Content authenticity proofs

ID: `content-authenticity-proofs`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/content-authenticity-proofs

### Problem

Digital media is trivially fakeable. A photo, video, or document circulating online has no widespread way to be checked against the source it claims, and the same authoring tools that produce convincing media also produce convincing fakes. Newsrooms whose footage is doctored, creators whose work is plagiarized or attributed to someone else, and viewers trying to figure out what is real all face the same problem with no shared answer.

### Solution

Media signed at the point of capture and through each subsequent edit, building an authenticity chain anyone can check. A photo, video, or document carries a verifiable trail back to the device or person that produced it, edits register against that record, and a fabrication shows up against the original signed content rather than competing with it on visual plausibility alone.

### Why Ethereum

An authenticity record only works if people who distrust each other can check it independently, and a registry run by one platform or government can be pressured to revoke signatures or favor certain sources. Recording the authenticity chain onchain keeps the history of who signed what verifiable by anyone, without the hosting platform having to cooperate or stay neutral.

---

## Content moderation

ID: `content-moderation`
Domains: Civil Society, Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/content-moderation

### Problem

Social platforms rely on centralized moderation teams and opaque algorithms to decide what is spam, manipulation, or harmful — systems that don't scale, lack accountability, and are trivially captured by political pressure. Reputation-weighted community moderation and verified-human signals exist as concepts but have no neutral infrastructure to run on that any platform could adopt.

### Solution

Modular moderation infrastructure combining community-written notes on contested content, reputation-weighted flagging where established accounts carry more signal, and stake-based curation where moderators put tokens at risk on their judgments — all running onchain so any platform can read them without building its own moderation stack from scratch.

### Why Ethereum

When moderation lives inside a single platform, that company alone decides what gets suppressed, and the system is easily captured by political pressure aimed at one chokepoint. Running reputation, stake records, and community notes onchain keeps the moderation signal outside any one company's control, so any platform can read the same signal and the rules behind it are inspectable and forkable by users.

## Cooperative and local marketplaces

ID: `cooperative-and-local-marketplaces`
Domains: Commerce, Food & Agriculture
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/cooperative-and-local-marketplaces

### Problem

Small producers selling through conventional distribution channels lose most of their margin to intermediaries, while consumers who want to buy local have no transparent, community-governed platform to connect with them directly.

### Solution

Community-owned platforms that let producers sell directly and keep more economic value within local food systems

### Why Ethereum

A conventional marketplace operator sets the fees, owns the reviews and customer relationships, and can suspend a producer or change the rules, leaving small sellers dependent on a platform whose interests differ from theirs. A neutral marketplace layer no single company controls lets producers participate without lock-in and keep their reputation and customer ties as something they own.

## Cooperative lending and liquidity pools

ID: `cooperative-lending-pools`
Domains: Finance, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/cooperative-lending-pools

### Problem

Small businesses, cooperatives, and credit unions lack mechanisms to pool reserves and share liquidity risk without expensive legacy banking infrastructure, forcing each member to maintain costly individual cash buffers.

### Solution

Blockchain-based cooperative finance that lets members pool capital, share liquidity, and access credit from one another — governed transparently and auditable by all participants.

### Why Ethereum

Pooling reserves through a bank or platform means an intermediary holds the pooled funds, sets the terms of access, and can freeze the pool or close it, while members have to trust its accounting. Running the pool onchain keeps the capital and its rules with the members who contributed it, and gives every participant an audit trail they can check themselves.

## Direct creator storefronts with programmable revenue splits

ID: `creator-storefronts`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/creator-storefronts

### Problem

A musician selling merchandise, a Substack writer selling a course, and an artist selling prints each route payments through 2–4 intermediary platforms that take 10–30% combined, add delays before creators can access funds, and give the creator no way to automatically share revenue with collaborators, producers, or the fans who helped grow their audience.

### Solution

Direct storefronts where revenue splits among collaborators, co-creators, and communities execute automatically at the moment of purchase — with instant settlement, programmable royalty flows, and no platform intermediary taking a cut of every transaction.

### Why Ethereum

When a storefront platform sits between a creator and their buyers, it sets the fees, holds the funds before releasing them, and can suspend the account or change the split at will. Building onchain keeps the storefront's payment logic and revenue terms in the creator's hands, where collaborators are paid by rules no operator can quietly rewrite.

## Credit scoring from off-chain financial history

ID: `credit-scoring`
Domains: Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/credit-scoring

### Problem

Hundreds of millions of people are creditworthy — they pay rent on time, maintain savings, and run profitable small businesses — but are invisible to formal lenders because their financial history lives in bank apps, rental platforms, and payroll systems that lenders can't access without the borrower surrendering raw account credentials.

### Solution

zkTLS-based credit assessments where borrowers prove specific financial claims — 12 months of on-time rent payments, a salary above a threshold, a business revenue history — directly from source platforms without sharing login credentials, giving lenders verifiable underwriting data for borrowers who lack formal credit files.

### Why Ethereum

A data aggregator standing between borrowers and lenders collects raw account credentials and financial history into one store that becomes a surveillance point and a breach target. Building this with zero-knowledge proofs onchain lets a borrower prove a specific claim, like a year of on-time rent, without handing over the underlying account, and keeps the check from being logged by a company in the middle.
