## Cross-border payroll and contractor payments

ID: `cross-border-payroll`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/cross-border-payroll

### Problem

Cross-border payroll and contractor payments route through multiple intermediaries, taking days to settle with high fees, while tax reporting and compliance for global teams remain a manual reconciliation nightmare.

### Solution

Payroll and contractor payments settled directly to workers onchain instead of routed through a chain of correspondent banks. The employer keeps control of the schedule and the funds, payouts arrive in minutes rather than days, and tax and KYC reporting is generated from the payment record instead of reconciled by hand across jurisdictions.

### Why Ethereum

Cross-border payroll routed through correspondent banks means each intermediary can delay, take a cut, or block a payment to a worker in a sanctioned-adjacent region, and the employer cannot see where money stalls. Running payouts onchain keeps the schedule and the funds under the employer's control and settles directly to workers without a chain of banks deciding whether the payment goes through.

---

## Curation markets

ID: `curation-markets`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/curation-markets

### Problem

Deciding what deserves attention, which research is worth reading, which products are worth buying, which emerging work is worth following, is done for free by people who carry the cost of being early and wrong and capture none of the value when they turn out to be right. The systems that aggregate those judgments are platform recommender engines that rank by undisclosed rules, or review and ratings systems that are cheap to game because a fake recommendation costs the recommender nothing. The people best placed to surface quality have no economic stake in their own accuracy.

### Solution

Curation markets let a person stake reputation or capital on a recommendation, earn a share when the pick is later borne out, and lose stake when it is not. Smart contracts settle payouts against a measurable outcome agreed in advance, such as audience growth, sales, citations, or downstream curation, and each curator builds a public track record tied to their address. The same primitive covers prediction markets on whether a piece of work will succeed and reputation-weighted feeds where curators with the strongest history surface higher. Because a wrong call costs the curator real stake, the signal is harder to fake than a free rating.

### Why Ethereum

A curation market works only if the payout rules cannot be quietly rewritten by whoever hosts it, and only if a curator can carry their track record with them when a better venue appears. Settling stakes, attribution, and payouts onchain makes the incentive structure legible to everyone taking part and keeps each curator's history portable across whatever discovery surfaces emerge. A platform-owned recommender can be switched off or retuned without notice; an open curation market keeps running as long as its contracts and its participants do.

---

## Customs records across borders

ID: `customs-records`
Domains: Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/customs-records

### Problem

Cross-border shipments are delayed at customs because each agency keeps clearance documents and compliance status in its own proprietary database, with no real-time view that the agencies on either side of a border can both read.

### Solution

Customs documents and compliance status anchored onchain as commitments, with the documents themselves held off-chain and checked against onchain merkle proofs. An agency on either side of a border verifies a shipment's clearance and tariff status against the same attestations instead of re-requesting paperwork, so clearance is not held up waiting for one party to confirm what another has already verified.

### Why Ethereum

A centralized customs system run by one vendor or one government puts a single operator in control of clearance for everyone, able to set access terms, see every shipment, or cut off a jurisdiction it disagrees with. Building it on neutral rails means no participating agency controls the system, and each can verify compliance status directly rather than trusting another party's database.

---

## Data assets

ID: `data-assets`
Domains: AI, Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/data-assets

### Problem

Valuable datasets have no standard way to be priced, packaged, or traded. Whether it is satellite imagery, industrial sensor telemetry, de-identified clinical records, or proprietary market data, the dataset changes hands through opaque brokers and bespoke NDA-driven deals where a buyer cannot verify quality or provenance. It cannot be combined with other datasets or posted as collateral the way a financial asset can.

### Solution

Datasets represented as onchain assets with licensing, metering, and revenue-split terms attached. They can be priced individually, combined into derived datasets (for example, a satellite feed merged with weather sensor data to produce a crop-yield estimate), traded, or used as collateral. Usage is recorded against the asset itself, so a data producer is paid by rules a buyer or broker cannot quietly revise.

### Why Ethereum

A data broker reports usage on its own, sets the prices, and can favor buyers it has relationships with, leaving data producers no way to check whether the royalties they receive match what was actually consumed. Representing data as an onchain asset keeps licensing terms and usage records verifiable by both sides, so producers are paid by rules the broker cannot quietly revise.

---

## Dataset provenance and reuse tracking

ID: `dataset-provenance-reuse-tracking`
Domains: Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/dataset-provenance-reuse-tracking

### Problem

Researchers who create high-quality datasets — curating, cleaning, and annotating data that takes months of work — receive almost no academic credit when other researchers use their data, because there's no reliable mechanism to track dataset reuse across papers and institutions. Simultaneously, researchers who want to build on prior work often can't verify whether a dataset has been altered since publication or confirm they're working with the same version that produced the original findings.

### Solution

A registry where published datasets are cryptographically fingerprinted at the time of deposit, with every subsequent access and citation recorded — so dataset creators receive verifiable credit proportional to actual reuse, and downstream researchers can confirm they're working with an unaltered version of the original data.

### Why Ethereum

A reuse registry held by one repository or publisher leaves dataset creators dependent on that operator to count citations fairly and keep serving the records, and it offers no independent way to confirm a dataset is unchanged. Fingerprinting data and recording access onchain keeps the citation trail outside any single operator's control and lets downstream researchers verify integrity themselves.

---

## Data integrity for decentralized clinical trials

ID: `decentralized-clinical-trials`
Domains: Health, Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/decentralized-clinical-trials

### Problem

Decentralized clinical trials let patients participate from home using wearables, symptom-reporting apps, and telemedicine, which means data is collected across hundreds of patient devices rather than at monitored investigator sites. That makes it harder for sponsors and regulators to be confident that electronic source data has not been altered, that consent was properly obtained, and that the chain of custody from device to database is intact.

### Solution

Each sensor reading, patient-reported outcome, and consent signature is hashed and timestamped at the moment it is captured. That creates an audit trail showing the data has not been changed since collection, giving monitors, sponsors, and regulators confidence in source data integrity without depending on physical site visits.

### Why Ethereum

When trial data lives in a sponsor-controlled database, the party with the most to gain from a positive result also holds the ability to alter source records, and regulators have to take the chain of custody on trust. Committing each reading and consent signature onchain at the moment of capture keeps the record verifiable by monitors and regulators without depending on the sponsor's cooperation.

---

## Decision markets for corporate governance

ID: `decision-markets-corporate-governance`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/decision-markets-corporate-governance

### Problem

Corporate decisions — which strategy to pursue, whether to hire or fire an executive, which product to prioritize — are made through a combination of politics, hierarchy, and intuition rather than mechanisms that aggregate genuine beliefs of those closest to the work. Board votes and management sign-off concentrate decision-making power in ways that reward confidence and seniority over accuracy, with no feedback loop that punishes bad predictions or rewards good ones. Organizations systematically act on what's good for those in power rather than what's good for the organization.

### Solution

Conditional prediction markets tied to company-specific metrics — share price, TVL, revenue, retention — where any proposal generates two parallel markets: expected metric outcome if it passes, and if it fails. The proposal executes if markets predict a positive impact. Participants with genuine information have financial incentive to trade accurately. Early implementations include Butter Markets (used in Optimism's grant allocation experiments) and MetaDAO, which has run 96+ proposals for 14 organizations using this mechanism.

### Why Ethereum

If the decision market runs on infrastructure that management controls, the people whose power the mechanism is meant to check can pause it, adjust how trades settle, or ignore a signal they dislike, which returns the decision to politics and seniority. Building it onchain keeps the market's rules and the link between its signal and the outcome verifiable by every participant, outside any single executive's reach.

---

## Delivery-triggered payments

ID: `delivery-triggered-payments`
Domains: Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/delivery-triggered-payments

### Problem

Suppliers and freight carriers wait weeks for payment after goods are delivered because reconciliation between shipping documents, invoices, and proof of delivery is manual, while carriers lack verifiable proof-of-location or proof-of-condition to trigger automatic settlement.

### Solution

Conditional release of funds tied to oracle-verified delivery events, proof-of-location, and proof-of-condition, automating settlement for both goods delivery and freight logistics

### Why Ethereum

When a buyer or a platform controls the system that decides when delivery counts as proven, the party that owes money also controls the trigger for paying it, and carriers wait while reconciliation drags. Building settlement onchain keeps the release conditions and the delivery record verifiable by both sides, so payment follows agreed proof rather than the payer's discretion.

---

## Dependency-graph funding

ID: `dependency-graph-funding`
Domains: Business Operations, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/dependency-graph-funding

### Problem

A maintainer whose library is depended on by thousands of downstream projects sees none of the economic value those projects generate. When a downstream company sponsors a project, the money stops at the top-level library and rarely reaches the upstream dependencies that project quietly relies on. The deepest layers of the stack, the cryptography libraries and parsers and build tools, are also the most under-resourced, because gratitude does not propagate down the import graph the way usage does.

### Solution

Funding contracts that fan an incoming sponsorship or revenue share across the dependency tree, weighted by usage proofs derived from package manifests and build artifacts. A downstream project receiving a grant or commercial revenue routes a configurable portion through the contract, which splits it among direct and transitive dependencies according to a rule the project's maintainers publish. Support reaches the layers it should without each upstream maintainer having to chase it manually.

### Why Ethereum

Routing money through a dependency graph requires every participant to agree on the same set of weights and the same set of recipient addresses, and to be confident that the routing logic cannot be quietly altered between deposit and payout. Settling the splits onchain, against a usage graph anyone can audit, lets a downstream maintainer commit to funding upstream work in a way her sponsors and her dependencies can both verify, without putting a foundation in the middle to mediate the relationship.

---

## Digital product passports

ID: `digital-product-passports`
Domains: Environment, Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/digital-product-passports

### Problem

The EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) mandates digital product passports for most goods sold in Europe by 2030 — but no neutral infrastructure exists for brands, recyclers, and regulators across supply chains to read and write to a common product record. Without it, origin and certification claims rely on paper trails that can be forged at every handoff, recycled materials lose their provenance once they re-enter supply chains, and secondhand buyers have no trustworthy way to verify repair history or remaining lifecycle value.

### Solution

Append-only product records that persist through every ownership transfer and material handoff — tracking origin, certifications, condition, repair history, and end-of-life status in a format any manufacturer, recycler, regulator, or secondhand buyer can read, satisfying ESPR requirements while making circular economy claims cryptographically verifiable rather than self-reported.

### Why Ethereum

If one company or industry body runs the product passport registry, it can shape what claims appear, revoke records, and gate which brands or recyclers may read and write. Keeping the product record on neutral rails means no single operator owns the history, so manufacturers, regulators, recyclers, and secondhand buyers can all verify origin and certification claims for themselves.

---

## Digital vehicle passports

ID: `digital-vehicle-passports`
Domains: Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/digital-vehicle-passports

### Problem

A vehicle's full history — manufacturing specs, ownership transfers, lien status, accident damage, and maintenance — is scattered across dealer records, insurance databases, and government registries that do not communicate, making title fraud and odometer rollback easy.

### Solution

End-to-end records covering manufacturing, ownership, liens, maintenance, accidents, and recycling — serving as both lifecycle passport and verifiable title

### Why Ethereum

A vehicle history service run by one company controls which records are shown, can be pressured to omit damage a dealer wants hidden, and leaves a buyer trusting a database they cannot inspect. Recording the lifecycle onchain keeps the chain of ownership and maintenance verifiable by anyone, so title fraud and odometer rollback show up against a record no single operator can quietly edit.

## Direct cash transfers and basic income distribution

ID: `direct-cash-transfer-programs`
Domains: Civil Society, Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/direct-cash-transfer-programs

### Problem

Billions of people without bank accounts cannot receive aid efficiently because traditional transfer systems depend on banking infrastructure and charge high fees through multiple intermediaries. Administering recurring universal basic income payments at scale adds a second layer of overhead: heavy bureaucratic processes for identity verification, eligibility checks, and distribution make such programs expensive to run and slow to reach recipients.

### Solution

Digital wallet-based transfer infrastructure that reaches unbanked populations directly at minimal cost — supporting both targeted aid disbursements and recurring automated payments, using decentralized identity and smart contracts to handle eligibility verification without centralized administrative overhead.

### Why Ethereum

When aid moves through banks and payment processors, those intermediaries take fees, decide who is allowed to receive funds, and can freeze or block transfers, leaving recipients dependent on institutions that may not serve them. Building distribution onchain lets funds reach anyone with a mobile wallet directly, and keeps the payment from being gated by a company or bank that can turn it off.

## Dispute resolution for contracts and freelance agreements

ID: `dispute-resolution`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/dispute-resolution

### Problem

Resolving disputes in B2B contracts and freelance agreements requires expensive, slow litigation or arbitrary platform support teams that apply opaque rules — pricing out individuals and small businesses from meaningful access to justice and leaving the outcome entirely in the hands of a platform that has its own interests.

### Solution

Decentralized arbitration mechanisms where specialized juror pools evaluate disputes using standardized evidence and structured deliberation — with jurors staking tokens on verdicts, outcomes enforced automatically via smart contract, and no ability for a losing party to delay compliance.

### Why Ethereum

When a platform resolves disputes among its own users, it applies rules it does not publish and reaches outcomes that serve its own interests, leaving the parties no way to check the process. Building arbitration onchain keeps the juror rules and the record of each verdict verifiable by both sides, so the outcome does not depend on trusting a support team that answers to the platform.

---

## Dynamic expense approvals

ID: `dynamic-expense-approvals`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/dynamic-expense-approvals

### Problem

Expense approval runs on static workflows in an ERP or expense tool: fixed dollar thresholds and fixed approver chains. The rule cannot tell whether a department is already over budget, whether the company's cash position has tightened, who is asking, or what the money is for. Companies end up either routing everything through finance, which is slow, or setting limits loose enough to be risky.

### Solution

Expense approvals where the rule is evaluated for each request against live inputs rather than read from a fixed table. The approval can depend on the requester's role and seniority, the department's remaining budget, the company's current cash position, the vendor and spend category, and oracle-fed external conditions. A recurring renewal under budget clears on its own, a new vendor or a purchase that pushes a team over its quarter is routed for review, and spending can tighten automatically when runway falls below a set level.

### Why Ethereum

An approval rule that reads the company's finances and outside conditions only works if those inputs cannot be quietly edited by whoever wants the payment to clear. Running the rule in the account itself, against onchain balances and oracle feeds, makes both the policy and the inputs it judges against inspectable, so a dynamic approval is something the organization can audit rather than a black box inside an expense tool.

---

## Earnouts and contingent payments

ID: `earnouts-contingent-payments`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/earnouts-contingent-payments

### Problem

In a lot of deals, part of the price is paid later, contingent on something happening: an M&A earnout tied to post-close revenue or EBITDA, a milestone holdback released on a regulatory approval or a key hire, a contingent value right that pays out if a clinical trial succeeds, an escrowed indemnity released on a future date. Once the deal closes, the party that owes the contingent payment usually controls the books, the operations, and the timing decisions that determine whether the trigger ever fires. The other side either trusts that accounting or litigates after the fact, and disputes over contingent payments are a common source of post-close conflict.

### Solution

A structure where contingent consideration is escrowed onchain and released according to a pre-agreed payout rule. The rule is tied to an objective metric verified by an agreed source, such as an auditor, payment rail, signed API record, platform usage feed, regulatory milestone, or other third-party attestation. Both sides can see the same rule, the same verification source, and the same payout conditions before closing.

### Why Ethereum

This is useful when the contingent payment depends on a metric both sides can define in advance and verify independently. Instead of leaving the payout entirely dependent on the paying party's later accounting, the parties can escrow funds, commit to a payout rule, and settle automatically when the agreed evidence is submitted. It does not eliminate the need for legal agreements or trusted data sources, but it does reduce post-close discretion, delay, and litigation leverage.

---

## Electronic Bill of Lading

ID: `electronic-bill-of-lading`
Domains: Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/electronic-bill-of-lading

### Problem

The bill of lading, the single most important document in international shipping, still circulates as a paper original that must be physically couriered between parties, causing delays and fraud risk.

### Solution

Replacing paper document of title with NFT-like digital representation of title and transfer rights

### Why Ethereum

An electronic bill of lading run on one provider's platform makes that company the registry of who holds title, able to set access terms, see every trade, or freeze a transfer, and the whole trade lane depends on it staying available. Building it on neutral rails keeps the document of title as an asset the holder controls directly, transferable and verifiable without any single operator's permission.

## Continuous environmental measurement and verification

ID: `environmental-measurement-and-verification`
Domains: Environment
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/environmental-measurement-and-verification

### Problem

Environmental claims — RECs, carbon intensity labels, ESG reports, biodiversity credits — rely on self-reported data with infrequent third-party audits, enabling double-counting and greenwashing. Biodiversity credits are especially vulnerable: a credit representing habitat that degraded a year after issuance looks identical to one representing thriving ecosystem, with no mechanism to flag or invalidate it when outcomes reverse.

### Solution

Continuous verification of environmental outcomes using IoT sensors, satellite imagery, acoustic monitoring, and remote sensing — with data logged onchain so that RECs, carbon credits, and biodiversity offsets carry cryptographic proof of their ongoing validity rather than depending on infrequent audits.

### Why Ethereum

Environmental claims today rest on data the issuer self-reports, and an auditor it pays can be dropped or pressured by the party it is supposed to check. Logging sensor and satellite data continuously onchain gives buyers and the public a measurement they can verify independently, and keeps a credit's record from being revised once an outcome reverses.

## Environmental-threshold enforcement

ID: `environmental-threshold-enforcement`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/environmental-threshold-enforcement

### Problem

Environmental rules like emissions limits and air-quality thresholds are often clear, but acting on them still needs human sign-off at each step. By the time a restriction or fine is issued, the pollution it was meant to address has already happened. Enforcement reliably lags the events it is supposed to govern.

### Solution

Environmental rules and their triggers executed as smart contracts. When oracle-verified sensor readings cross a legal threshold, the consequence executes on its own, whether that is a traffic restriction during a pollution spike, a fine for an emissions breach, or a suspended permit. Enforcement keeps pace with the readings instead of waiting on a decision at each step.

### Why Ethereum

If the rules and their enforcement ran on a system one agency controlled, that agency could quietly change the logic or apply it selectively, favoring some polluters over others. Publishing the thresholds and their triggers onchain keeps them inspectable by anyone, so the public can confirm enforcement runs by the same rule it can read.

---

## Cross-network EV charging roaming settlement

ID: `ev-charging-coordination`
Domains: Utilities
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ev-charging-coordination

### Problem

When an EV driver charges on a network other than their home provider, the roaming transaction passes through bilateral settlement agreements between the charge point operator (CPO) and the eMobility service provider (eMSP) — each pair requiring a custom integration. In Europe alone there are 500+ CPOs and dozens of eMSPs, and the bilateral model means most roaming pairs simply don't exist, leaving drivers unable to charge on large portions of the network without creating new accounts.

### Solution

A neutral settlement layer where any CPO and any eMSP can clear roaming transactions without bilateral agreements — using standardized session records (kWh delivered, time, location, tariff) that both parties confirm onchain, with payment executing automatically at session close.

### Why Ethereum

If a single clearinghouse owned the roaming layer, it would decide which operators get to connect and could price its position as the chokepoint every charging session passes through. Settling sessions on neutral rails lets any operator and any provider clear with each other directly, and the rules of settlement are inspectable by all of them rather than set by one company.

## Event tickets with resale rights

ID: `event-ticket-resale`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/event-ticket-resale

### Problem

Event ticketing is plagued by scalper bots, counterfeit tickets, and opaque resale markets where venues and artists lose control over pricing and capture none of the secondary-market value.

### Solution

Resalable access to events, concerts, and festivals

### Why Ethereum

A centralized ticket platform sits between fans and artists, sets the fees, runs an opaque resale market, and keeps the secondary value while venues lose control over their own pricing. Issuing tickets onchain keeps the resale rules and royalty splits with the venues and artists who set them, and lets fans verify a ticket is genuine without trusting whichever company happens to run the platform.

## Fan-funded media with governance rights

ID: `fan-funded-media`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/fan-funded-media

### Problem

Independent filmmakers, musicians, and journalists must either sign away creative control or run crowdfunding campaigns on platforms that offer backers no governance rights, transparent fund allocation, or financial upside in the work's success.

### Solution

Onchain funding and governance for films, music, and journalism — where backers hold tokens that represent both financial participation and voting rights over creative decisions.

### Why Ethereum

A crowdfunding platform decides which projects are allowed to raise, what rights backers actually get, and whether promised payouts ever arrive, and it can change those terms or drop a project to manage its own risk. Building onchain keeps the funding terms and governance rights with the creators and backers, recorded where anyone can check them and no host can revoke them.

## Film and TV residual payments

ID: `film-tv-residuals`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/film-tv-residuals

### Problem

When a film or show is reused, streamed in a new window, licensed to another territory, or rerun, the actors, writers, and directors are owed residuals. Those payments are calculated and disbursed by studios and distributors from their own records of where and how often a title ran. Performers cannot see the underlying usage data, residual statements arrive long after the exhibition they cover, and underpayment is common enough that the guilds run standing audit programs to recover it.

### Solution

Residual terms encoded against verified distribution and streaming data, so that when a title runs in a new window the payment owed to each rights holder is computed and released from the same usage record everyone can see. A performer gets a residual that follows the actual exhibition of their work rather than a statement they have to take on trust.

### Why Ethereum

The studio or distributor that owes residuals is also the only party that records where and how often a title ran, so performers audit blind and chase payments well after the fact. Settling residuals onchain against verified distribution data puts the usage record and the payment rule where the guild and the performer can verify them directly, so a residual does not depend on the payer's own accounting.

---

## Firearm licensing and registration

ID: `firearm-licensing-registration`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/firearm-licensing-registration

### Problem

State firearm licensing (permit-to-purchase, FOID cards, concealed-carry permits) and state-level firearm registration sit in siloed, often paper-based systems that do not move with the holder across jurisdictions. A licensee crossing state lines, a transfer between residents of different states, or a buyer at a gun show in another state all run into systems that cannot verify each other's records, while federal law blocks the kind of centralized registry that would otherwise paper over the gap.

### Solution

Firearm licenses and registration records issued by states as verifiable credentials the holder carries, with selective disclosure so a check exposes only the specific fact in question, such as that a license is current and unrevoked. Verification anchors against the issuing state's signing key onchain, so a counterparty in another state can confirm a record without that state running a lookup service or anyone maintaining a federal database.

### Why Ethereum

A national firearm registry is politically blocked, and a single searchable database of who owns what could be queried, leaked, or weaponized. Issuing licenses and registration records as holder-controlled credentials, verifiable against state signing keys onchain, lets the system work across jurisdictions without any party maintaining the kind of central database the law forbids.

## Food provenance and traceability

ID: `food-provenance-and-traceability`
Domains: Food & Agriculture, Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/food-provenance-and-traceability

### Problem

When a food safety recall is issued, tracing contaminated product back to the source takes days or weeks because lot IDs change at every handoff between grower, packer, distributor, and retailer — each maintaining their own disconnected records — meaning contaminated product stays on shelves while investigators manually reconstruct the chain.

### Solution

A common lot ID standard that persists immutably through every handoff in the supply chain — so when a retailer scans a product, they can trace it back to the specific farm field and harvest date in seconds, and a recall can be executed against a precise subset of product rather than pulling entire categories from shelves.

### Why Ethereum

A traceability platform run by one large retailer or distributor would let that operator decide who sees the chain and could quietly edit records that point back to its own suppliers. Recording each handoff onchain keeps the history outside any one company's control, so a recall can be traced and food fraud caught by anyone in the chain rather than only the host.

## Fund flows and disaster relief coordination

ID: `fund-flows-disaster-relief`
Domains: Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/fund-flows-disaster-relief

### Problem

Charitable donations, advocacy grants, and international aid flow through opaque intermediary chains where funds are lost to corruption, misallocation, or overhead — with donors unable to verify money reached its intended recipients. After disasters this compounds: dozens of NGOs and agencies respond simultaneously with no joint view of who received what, duplicating aid in accessible areas while remote communities get nothing.

### Solution

Onchain tracking of fund flows from donor to final recipient with real-time visibility and audit logs — combined with onchain coordination infrastructure for disaster response that lets all responding organizations see disbursements, supply distribution, and beneficiary verification in a single view.

### Why Ethereum

When aid flows through intermediaries that report on themselves, donors see only what each organization chooses to disclose, and no responding agency has a joint view to coordinate against. Recording disbursements onchain keeps the trail visible to donors and responders alike, so contributions can be followed to the recipient without trusting any single organization's books.

---

## Futarchy for public policy

ID: `futarchy-public-policy`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/futarchy-public-policy

### Problem

Democratic systems are good at aggregating what citizens want but systematically bad at determining which policies will actually deliver it. Voters choose representatives based on stated intentions; representatives vote on bills based on lobbying, ideology, and coalition politics rather than evidence of likely impact. Expert panels and think tanks aggregate some information but lack skin in the game — a consultant who recommends a bad policy faces no financial consequence.

### Solution

A governance layer that separates the question of values (decided democratically: what should we optimize for?) from the question of means (decided by markets: which policy will best achieve it?). Elected representatives define a measurable welfare metric — GDP, life expectancy, emissions index — and conditional prediction markets determine which policies are expected to raise it. A policy becomes law only when market estimates clearly predict it will improve welfare relative to the status quo. Robin Hanson's original formulation ('vote on values, bet on beliefs') has been live-tested by MetaDAO for DAO governance and explored by at least one government health agency since 2024.

### Why Ethereum

If the market that decides policy ran on government-controlled infrastructure, the officials being judged could pause trading, exclude participants, or quietly discard a signal that went against them. Running the markets onchain keeps the prices and the welfare metric outside the control of the people they constrain, where any citizen can audit them and the mechanism keeps running without anyone's permission.

---

## Harvest pre-financing for smallholder farmers

ID: `harvest-pre-financing`
Domains: Food & Agriculture, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/harvest-pre-financing

### Problem

A subsistence farmer who needs $300 to buy seeds and fertilizer at planting time has no collateral for a bank loan and no trading history with formal lenders — so they borrow from local moneylenders at 60–100% annual interest rates, or go without inputs and accept a lower yield, trapping them in a cycle where they can never accumulate enough surplus to escape the next season's dependency.

### Solution

Pre-harvest financing backed by tokenized future crop receipts — letting farmers collateralize their standing crop against verified planting data, weather feeds, and historical yield records, with repayment automatically deducted from the proceeds when the harvest is sold.

### Why Ethereum

When financing runs through a single lender or platform, that operator sets the terms, holds the records, and can cut a farmer off or change the rules with no recourse, much as local moneylenders already do. Running the crop receipts and repayment onchain lets any lender extend credit against the same verifiable collateral, and the loan terms stay legible to the farmer instead of locked inside one provider's system.

---

## Metering and paying home energy devices for grid flexibility

ID: `home-energy-grid-flexibility`
Domains: Utilities
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/home-energy-grid-flexibility

### Problem

Home energy devices like batteries, smart thermostats, EV chargers, and water heaters can shift or reduce their load to help balance the grid, and utilities increasingly need that flexibility. There is no scalable way to meter what each individual device contributed and pay its owner for it. Every device runs a different protocol, and the contribution of any single home is too small for grid operators to track and settle on its own, so the flexibility goes uncompensated and underused.

### Solution

A settlement layer that meters the load reduction each device delivers, verifies it against the home's smart meter baseline, and pays the device owner automatically. By pooling many small contributions into one verifiable record, it makes it practical for aggregators to enroll millions of household devices and compensate each one for the flexibility it provides.

### Why Ethereum

An aggregator that meters device contributions and also pays for them reports on its own performance, and device owners have no independent way to confirm the demand reductions credited to them were measured honestly. Building the settlement layer onchain keeps the metering rules and the payment record verifiable by owners and regulators, so compensation does not rest on trusting the aggregator's books.

---

## Hyperstition markets

ID: `hyperstition-markets`
Domains: Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/hyperstition-markets

### Problem

Many valuable outcomes require enough people to act at once that no individual will move first. A new protocol reaching adoption, a local currency achieving network effects, a civic technology deployed across a city: each needs distributed, multi-actor commitment. Traditional crowdfunding pools money for a single project but cannot coordinate that kind of contribution, and prediction markets aggregate beliefs about what will happen without creating the conditions for it.

### Solution

Markets designed to coordinate an outcome rather than only forecast it. Buying YES stakes a participant financially in making the prediction come true, and the public price acts as a Schelling point: as more people buy YES, the rising price signals growing collective commitment and rewards the early believers who do the hard coordination work over late arrivals. The aim is to help an ecosystem tip, such as a new protocol reaching adoption or a civic technology getting deployed widely. Vitalik Buterin has flagged real manipulation risks here, including a 'hitman problem' where actors profit from causing bad outcomes and whale concentration that engineers a result rather than letting it emerge.

### Why Ethereum

A hyperstition market run by one company would leave that operator deciding who counts as a contributor, when the market resolves, and whether early believers actually get paid, which undercuts the coordination the market is meant to create. Running it onchain keeps the prices, the resolution rules, and the payouts outside any operator's hands, where participants can verify them and connect the market to other attestation systems without asking permission.

---

## Impact certificates with retroactive outcome verification

ID: `impact-certificates`
Domains: Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/impact-certificates

### Problem

Social-impact funders have no reliable way to verify that grant-funded programs delivered promised outcomes — a job training program reports 80% placement rates, but the funder has no independent mechanism to confirm these numbers, and the incentive structure rewards narrative over evidence because future grants depend on reported (not verified) impact.

### Solution

Tokenized impact certificates that represent verified outcomes — issued when an independent evaluator confirms results (e.g., verified job placements, measured emissions reductions, confirmed housing placements) — creating tradeable assets that retroactive funders can purchase to reward proven impact, aligning incentives so that programs that actually deliver attract more capital than programs that report well.

### Why Ethereum

If impact certificates lived on a platform owned by one funder or registry, that operator could decide which outcomes count and which funders are allowed to buy in, recreating the gatekeeping the model is meant to remove. Issuing them onchain keeps the certificates outside any single funder's control, so the same verified outcome can attract capital from many sources and anyone can check what a certificate represents.

---

## Informal land tenure formalization

ID: `informal-land-tenure-formalization`
Domains: Government, Real Estate & Housing
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/informal-land-tenure-formalization

### Problem

In much of the developing world, the majority of land is held under customary or informal tenure with no formal title. Families have lived on, farmed, and built on land for generations under arrangements recognized locally but not in any registry that a bank, court, or buyer outside the community would accept. Without verifiable title, the holder cannot use the land as collateral, sell to a buyer outside the immediate community, or defend the claim in court if a more powerful party tries to take it. Hernando de Soto's estimate of the resulting "dead capital" runs into the trillions.

### Solution

Tenure records anchored against the actual chain of possession: witness attestations from neighbors, dated photos and surveys, signoffs from local authorities, rather than a court-issued title that does not exist. A community-recognized claim becomes a record a bank or counterparty outside the community can verify, without the holder having to retrofit a paper-title history that was never created.

### Why Ethereum

Land registries run by single governments or vendors in places without strong institutions are exactly where title fraud and land grabs happen, because the people in charge of the record are also the ones with reason to alter it. Anchoring tenure onchain keeps the record outside any one office's reach, so a family's claim does not depend on a particular government continuing to honor it, and a buyer or lender can verify provenance independent of the registry that issued it.

---

## Insurance claims adjudication

ID: `insurance-claims-adjudication`
Domains: Insurance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/insurance-claims-adjudication

### Problem

Insurance companies face hundreds of disputed claims monthly that don't fit automated processing rules — ambiguous coverage questions, contested damage assessments, conflicting evidence — and route them through traditional arbitration that takes 7–10 days, costs hundreds of dollars per case, and produces outcomes neither party finds credible.

### Solution

Specialized juror pools that evaluate disputed insurance claims using standardized evidence packages and structured deliberation protocols — with jurors staking tokens on their verdicts, outcomes determined by stake-weighted consensus, and payment executing automatically once adjudication is complete.

### Why Ethereum

When an insurer runs or hires the body that adjudicates its own disputed claims, the party with the conflict of interest controls the process, and the claimant has little way to know the deliberation was fair. Building adjudication onchain keeps the juror rules and the record of each verdict verifiable by both sides, so the outcome does not depend on trusting a panel the insurer can influence.

---

## Cross-party inventory verification and inventory-backed lending

ID: `inventory-verification-lending`
Domains: Logistics & Trade, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/inventory-verification-lending

### Problem

Lenders offering inventory financing have no independent way to verify that pledged inventory actually exists, hasn't been double-pledged to another lender, and matches the borrower's representations — a $600B+ market plagued by warehouse receipt fraud (e.g., the Qingdao metals scandal where the same copper and aluminum were pledged to multiple banks simultaneously). The underlying issue is that inventory records across warehouses, suppliers, and retailers are maintained in disconnected systems with no single source of truth.

### Solution

Tokenized warehouse receipts linked to verified physical inventory — with each receipt representing a specific lot in a specific warehouse, ownership transferable onchain, and double-pledging detectable by any lender checking the onchain record before extending credit.

### Why Ethereum

A warehouse receipt system run by one operator leaves lenders trusting whoever maintains the database, and the Qingdao scandal showed how easily disconnected records hide the same inventory pledged many times. Putting receipts onchain gives every lender the same ownership record to check independently, so a receipt cannot be quietly handed to two parties and no one operator controls what the books say.

---

## Invoice and receivables financing

ID: `invoice-receivables-financing`
Domains: Finance, Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/invoice-receivables-financing

### Problem

Small businesses and exporters wait 30-90 days for payment on legitimate invoices and receivables, while factoring intermediaries charge steep discount rates and lenders reject applications because documents are unverifiable PDFs prone to double-pledging.

### Solution

Tokenized invoices and receivables that can be verified, sold, collateralized, or traded in real time, so a business can raise cash against money it is owed without waiting out the payment term. A lender checks the same ownership record everyone else sees, which is what stops a single receivable from being pledged to several lenders at once.

### Why Ethereum

When invoices are PDFs and factoring runs through one intermediary, lenders depend on that intermediary's word and the same receivable can be pledged to several of them at once. Putting invoices onchain gives every lender the same ownership record to verify directly, so authenticity does not rest on a single platform and the same invoice cannot be sold twice.

---

## IP assets

ID: `ip-assets`
Domains: Finance, Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ip-assets

### Problem

Intellectual property rights are indivisible and illiquid, making it nearly impossible for small investors to participate in IP financing, for researchers to crowdfund early-stage IP, or for inventors to unlock the dormant value of their portfolios.

### Solution

Fractional ownership, crowdfunding, financing, and trading of intellectual property rights through IP-NFTs and tokenized IP instruments

### Why Ethereum

A platform that hosts fractional IP shares controls who can buy in, what trades clear, and which projects get listed, and it can delist an asset or freeze a market to protect its own interests. Issuing these rights onchain keeps ownership records and transfers outside any one operator's reach, so inventors and small investors hold positions that stay tradable without asking permission.

## IP registration and prior art

ID: `ip-registration-prior-art`
Domains: Science, Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ip-registration-prior-art

### Problem

Creators proving when a work was made and inventors establishing priority in patent disputes both rely on slow, expensive government registries that vary by jurisdiction and are vulnerable to retroactive challenge. Inventors lack a tamper-proof way to timestamp lab notebooks and experimental data, while creators have no instant, cross-jurisdictional proof of authorship that doesn't require navigating multiple national systems.

### Solution

Immutable, cryptographically timestamped records for both creative works and inventions — establishing proof of creation, authorship, and prior art at the moment of registration, verifiable instantly across jurisdictions without filing separately in each one.

### Why Ethereum

A registry run by one office or company decides which records stand, can be pressured to backdate or revoke entries, and leaves creators dependent on its goodwill across every jurisdiction. Recording a timestamp on neutral rails keeps the proof of when a work existed verifiable by anyone, with no operator able to alter the history after the fact.

## Source protection for journalists

ID: `journalist-source-protection`
Domains: Media, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/journalist-source-protection

### Problem

A government whistleblower who wants to leak to a journalist faces a dilemma: submitting documents anonymously makes the story hard to verify and easy to dismiss, while providing proof of their insider status — job title, department, access level — makes them identifiable and exposes them to prosecution.

### Solution

Zero-knowledge systems where sources prove their organizational affiliation — that they work at a specific agency or hold a specific clearance level — without revealing their identity, generating a cryptographic attestation that journalists can publish to establish credibility without burning the source.

### Why Ethereum

A verification service run by a company would hold records linking sources to the credentials they proved, a single place that can be subpoenaed, breached, or pressured to expose a whistleblower. Building this with zero-knowledge proofs onchain lets a source prove their role without that link existing anywhere, so a journalist can publish credible proof and nothing about the source's identity is stored for anyone to compel.

## Privacy-preserving KYC and sanctions screening proofs

ID: `kyc-sanctions-proofs`
Domains: Business Operations, Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/kyc-sanctions-proofs

### Problem

Every financial institution that onboards the same customer independently collects and stores the same identity documents, running redundant KYC checks that cost $50–500 per customer — while creating dozens of copies of sensitive identity data across institutions that each become breach targets. Cross-border transactions compound the problem: a European bank processing a payment to a US correspondent must demonstrate OFAC and EU sanctions compliance, which currently requires sharing enough customer data for the counterparty to independently screen — forcing a choice between privacy and compliance.

### Solution

Zero-knowledge proofs that let institutions demonstrate a customer passed KYC and sanctions screening — proving the fact of compliance without sharing the underlying identity documents, so counterparties can satisfy their regulatory obligations without receiving (and storing) sensitive data they didn't need.

### Why Ethereum

The current process forces a customer's identity documents to be copied into every institution that onboards them, leaving sensitive data scattered across many breach targets and copied to each counterparty. Zero-knowledge proofs onchain let an institution show that screening was done without handing over the underlying records, so the data stays with the customer rather than accumulating wherever a transaction goes.

---

## Land trust and housing co-op coordination

ID: `land-trust-housing-coop-coordination`
Domains: Real Estate & Housing, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/land-trust-housing-coop-coordination

### Problem

Land trusts and housing cooperatives are structured as 501(c)(3)s or limited equity co-ops, with governance rules buried in paper bylaws that members rarely read, share transfers processed through manual legal work, and financial reporting that requires expensive annual audits. The overhead scales linearly with the number of units and makes it prohibitively expensive to operate community-owned housing at anything beyond neighborhood scale.

### Solution

A governance and ownership coordination layer that sits on top of existing legal entities. Membership transfers automate within the constraints of the ground lease or co-op agreement, governance votes and financial reporting are verifiable to members in real time, and the per-unit administrative overhead drops to a level that lets CLT and co-op structures scale.

### Why Ethereum

When a land trust or co-op runs on paper bylaws and outside administrators, members rarely see how governance and money actually move, and they depend on staff or a vendor to process transfers and report honestly. Putting the coordination layer onchain lets members verify votes and distributions directly, keeping control of the organization with the people who belong to it.

## Letters of credit

ID: `letters-of-credit`
Domains: Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/letters-of-credit

### Problem

A letter of credit — the bank guarantee that an importer will pay an exporter on delivery — still requires physical paper documents to be couriered between banks across countries, a process that takes 5–10 days and costs $500–1500 per transaction for what is fundamentally a message saying 'we guarantee payment if these conditions are met.'

### Solution

Smart contract-based letters of credit that issue, transfer, and settle digitally — releasing payment to the exporter automatically when shipping documents and delivery conditions are cryptographically verified, without physical document exchange.

### Why Ethereum

A digital letter-of-credit network owned by one bank or consortium would let those operators decide who can issue and clear, and route every trade through infrastructure they control and price. Running letters of credit onchain keeps the guarantee and its conditions outside any single institution's hands, so any bank can participate and counterparties can verify the terms themselves rather than trusting a courier and an intermediary.

## Local infrastructure bonds

ID: `local-infrastructure-bonds`
Domains: Finance, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/local-infrastructure-bonds

### Problem

Neighborhoods that want to collectively fund a solar array, community broadband network, or local community center have no mechanism to issue bonds to residents — municipal bond markets require expensive intermediaries and high minimums that exclude small projects and the residents who would benefit most from investing in their own community. Rural areas without broadband are particularly affected: incumbent telecoms won't build where returns are uncertain, while community-owned networks can't access upfront capital.

### Solution

Tokenized community bonds that let residents invest as little as $10 in specific local infrastructure projects — solar, broadband, community spaces — with coupon payments automated via smart contract and milestone-verified fund release ensuring projects are built before capital is fully deployed.

### Why Ethereum

Routing community bonds through a financial intermediary means an outside party holds the record, controls the minimums that price residents out, and can change terms or wind the program down. Building onchain keeps the bond's rules and the record of who is owed what with the community, verifiable by every resident and not dependent on a single firm staying in business.

## Batch and quality records for manufacturing

ID: `manufacturing-batch-records`
Domains: Logistics & Trade, Health
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/manufacturing-batch-records

### Problem

Pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers need batch records that regulators and partners can trust, but most store them in mutable databases where a quality engineer can change a test result after the fact without anyone noticing. Reconciling records across suppliers for a single product lot takes weeks of manual document retrieval, which slows recalls when speed matters most.

### Solution

Batch records that capture every production step, quality test, and deviation with cryptographic attestation at the moment of recording. The record cannot be revised afterward, and lot-level history can be traced across the whole supplier chain instantly when a recall is triggered.

### Why Ethereum

When batch records sit in a manufacturer's own mutable database, the company being audited controls the evidence and a quality result can be changed after the fact without anyone noticing. Committing each production step onchain puts the record beyond the manufacturer's reach to revise, so regulators and partners get an audit trail that holds because of how it is built rather than because a procedure was followed.

## Milestone-based scholarship and grant disbursement

ID: `milestone-scholarship-disbursement`
Domains: Finance, Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/milestone-scholarship-disbursement

### Problem

Education grants and scholarships from foundations, governments, and endowments are disbursed upfront with minimal accountability for outcomes — a foundation funding 200 scholarships across 50 institutions has no programmatic way to verify that recipients maintained enrollment, completed required coursework, or met GPA thresholds before the next tranche is released, relying instead on self-reported status updates from institutions that have financial incentive to retain enrolled students regardless of progress.

### Solution

Smart contract-governed scholarship funds that release tuition payments in tranches tied to institution-attested milestones — enrollment verification, credit completion, GPA maintenance — with transparent reporting to funders on aggregate outcomes across their entire portfolio.

### Why Ethereum

When disbursement runs through a single administrator, funders rely on self-reported status from institutions that have a financial reason to keep drawing funds whether or not students are progressing. Building the scholarship fund onchain keeps the release conditions and the record of each milestone and payment verifiable by funders directly, so accountability does not rest on trusting the institution's own reporting.

## Mortgage & home-equity rails

ID: `mortgage-home-equity-rails`
Domains: Real Estate & Housing, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/mortgage-home-equity-rails

### Problem

Mortgage servicing and secondary market trading depend on legacy systems with slow reconciliation, making loan transfers error-prone and limiting borrower access to competitive terms.

### Solution

Servicing and secondary markets become programmable, traceable and accessible

### Why Ethereum

When servicing and secondary trading run on the private systems of a few large institutions, borrowers cannot see who holds their loan or whether terms were applied correctly, and the records can be reconciled in ways they never observe. Putting the loan and its servicing logic onchain keeps the obligation auditable by the borrower and tradable without permission from a gatekeeper.

## Music sync licensing

ID: `music-sync-licensing`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/music-sync-licensing

### Problem

A filmmaker, YouTuber, or advertiser who wants to license a song for their production must either navigate months-long negotiations with major labels — who often decline small requests entirely — or use generic royalty-free music, because there's no scalable way for independent artists to make their catalog licensable at standardized rates.

### Solution

A licensing registry where artists pre-set terms and prices for different use types — YouTube video, short film, TV ad, podcast — so any buyer can instantly purchase a sync license with automatic payment to all rights holders, without negotiation or a licensing intermediary.

### Why Ethereum

A licensing intermediary decides whose catalog is listed, what a license costs, and when co-writers and producers are paid, and it can hold funds or drop an artist on its own terms. Building the registry onchain keeps the licensing terms and the record of who is owed what with the rights holders, where any buyer can verify a license and payment follows rules no administrator controls.

## Open-source contribution records and funding

ID: `open-source-contribution-funding`
Domains: Civil Society, Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/open-source-contribution-funding

### Problem

Open-source contributors build critical infrastructure but have no portable record of their contributions, and funding decisions are made by a small number of gatekeepers disconnected from the people doing the work.

### Solution

A portable record of who contributed what to open-source projects, with funding that flows against that record rather than through a handful of gatekeepers. Contributors carry their history across projects and platforms, and any funder can direct money toward the work using the same record, with reward flows that are visible to everyone.

### Why Ethereum

When contribution history and funding decisions sit inside one platform or with a few gatekeepers, that party decides whose work counts and can deplatform a contributor or steer money toward favored projects. Keeping contribution records and governance onchain lets the people doing the work carry their history anywhere, and any funder can recognize it without a central authority's approval.

## Opportunity markets

ID: `opportunity-markets`
Domains: AI
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/opportunity-markets

### Problem

People with deep contextual expertise — a music fan who spots an unsigned artist, a researcher who recognizes a breakthrough paper, a local supplier who notices a successful business before investors — have valuable information but no institutional connections and no mechanism to monetize their insight. Traditional scout programs can't scale beyond the institution's ability to vet scouts and recommendations. Public prediction markets don't work either: for a scout to profit, someone must lose an offsetting amount — and no market maker wants to bet against thousands of opportunities they've never heard of. If an institution subsidizes liquidity publicly, competitors free-ride on the same signal.

### Solution

Private prediction markets where a sponsor (a label, VC, hiring firm) provides liquidity against outcomes like 'will we sign Artist X?' — but keeps prices visible only to themselves during an opportunity window of roughly two weeks. Anyone can create a market for any opportunity and stake their conviction. As scouts buy YES and drive prices up, the sponsor sees a rising private signal and investigates. If they act and the outcome resolves positively, the scout is paid automatically. After the window closes, positions become public. Designed by Dave White and Matt Liston (Paradigm, August 2025).

Source: [Opportunity Markets, Paradigm 2025](https://www.paradigm.xyz/2025/08/opportunity-markets)

### Why Ethereum

If the sponsor ran the market on its own system, it would control the prices, the resolution, and the payout, and an outside scout would have no way to know their signal was used or their stake honored. Running it onchain keeps payouts bound to the resolution rule and makes the trades auditable once the window closes, so a sponsor cannot quietly exploit information a scout surfaced.

---

## Outcome-based funding for social services

ID: `outcome-based-funding`
Domains: Civil Society, Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/outcome-based-funding

### Problem

Large social service contracts — for housing, job placement, addiction recovery — are paid upfront with no enforceable link between disbursement and delivery. Funders have no programmatic way to verify that contracted metrics like bed occupancy, assessment completions, or housing placements were actually achieved before releasing the next payment tranche.

### Solution

Smart contracts that release payments to service providers only when verified metrics are independently confirmed — turning outcome-based contracting from a legal aspiration into a structural property of how funds flow.

### Why Ethereum

When a funder both disburses money and judges whether outcomes were met, political pressure or a comfortable relationship with a provider can loosen the link between payment and delivery, and the public cannot see where the gap opened. Putting the release rule onchain keeps the conditions and the verification visible to everyone, so funds flow against confirmed results rather than a funder's discretion.

---

## Parametric health insurance payouts

ID: `parametric-health-insurance`
Domains: Insurance, Health
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/parametric-health-insurance

### Problem

Many health insurance claims have simple, verifiable trigger conditions. A policyholder is admitted to a hospital, or completes a covered preventive visit, and is clearly eligible for a payout. These claims still move through the same weeks-long adjudication pipeline as complex cases that need medical review, adding administrative cost and delay to products whose whole value is paying out quickly during a health event.

### Solution

Parametric health benefit products where a payout triggers automatically once a standardized medical event is attested, such as a hospital admission confirmed by the facility or a logged preventive visit. Claims that do not need utilization review or a medical necessity determination settle within hours instead of weeks.

### Why Ethereum

When the insurer alone controls the claims pipeline, it has an incentive to slow or deny payouts on products whose value depends on speed, and the policyholder has little recourse. Encoding the trigger conditions onchain means a clearly eligible event pays out on terms both sides agreed to in advance, without the payer being able to add friction after the fact.

---

## Parametric weather insurance for farmers

ID: `parametric-weather-insurance`
Domains: Food & Agriculture, Insurance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/parametric-weather-insurance

### Problem

Smallholder farmers in climate-vulnerable regions need weather insurance but manual claims processing takes weeks, requires costly adjusters who can't economically serve small policies, and produces disputes that erode trust in the product. Traditional underwriters also reject farmers who lack formal production records, even when satellite and weather data could substitute.

### Solution

Parametric insurance products for farmers triggered automatically by satellite imagery and weather station data — when rainfall or temperature readings cross pre-agreed thresholds indicating crop loss, payouts execute without a claim form or adjuster, making it economically viable to serve smallholders at scale.

### Why Ethereum

When an insurer controls both the policy terms and the decision to pay, a smallholder has little recourse if claims are delayed or denied, and the underwriter has every incentive to stall. Putting the payout rule onchain lets the trigger and the data feeding it stay visible to the farmer, so settlement does not depend on a company choosing to honor it.

## Participatory budgeting in local government

ID: `participatory-budgeting`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/participatory-budgeting

### Problem

Participatory budgeting lets residents propose and vote on how a portion of their local budget should be spent, but the process usually runs through paper ballots, ad-hoc websites, or proprietary platforms that the city pays a vendor to operate. Residents have no independent way to verify that their proposals were registered, their votes were counted as cast, or the resulting allocations actually matched the winning proposals once the budget is later executed.

### Solution

A participatory budgeting system where proposals, votes, and final allocations are recorded onchain, with verifiable ballot inclusion using zero-knowledge proofs. A resident can confirm their proposal was registered and their vote counted, the city can show the winning projects tied to actual disbursements, and the connection between what was voted on and what was funded is auditable end to end.

### Why Ethereum

When a city runs participatory budgeting through a contracted vendor or its own database, the body whose spending is being constrained also controls the record of what residents chose, and any inconvenient outcome could be quietly adjusted or lost between the vote and the budget. Recording proposals, votes, and disbursements onchain keeps the chain from input to execution verifiable by residents directly, so the city's commitment to funding what people voted for becomes structural rather than discretionary.

---

## Patient-controlled health records

ID: `patient-controlled-health-records`
Domains: Health, Identity
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/patient-controlled-health-records

### Problem

Medical records are siloed across hospitals, clinics, and insurers — leaving patients unable to access, control, or share their own health data when switching providers or seeking second opinions. The problem is acute for mental health: a patient switching therapists must reconstruct their entire psychiatric history from memory — medications that worked, dosages that caused side effects, previous diagnoses — because clinician notes have no standard format and no patient-controlled transfer mechanism.

### Solution

Systems that give patients direct control over their medical data in a standardized portable format — enabling secure sharing across providers, granular consent over which details are disclosed, and verifiable attestation of test results and clinical findings that can't be silently altered.

### Why Ethereum

When records sit in hospital and insurer systems, the institution decides what a patient can access and when, and a central store of medical histories becomes a target for breaches and surveillance. Building patient-controlled records onchain keeps consent and access with the patient, lets any provider verify a record was not altered, and avoids routing sensitive history through a company that can log it.

---

## Pay-per-use micropayments

ID: `pay-per-use-micropayments`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/pay-per-use-micropayments

### Problem

Today's payment rails have an economic floor. Cards cannot profitably process anything below roughly $0.50 because the fixed per-transaction cost eats the margin, which blocks entire pricing models that would otherwise make sense: paying a few cents to read one article, paying per API call instead of buying into a subscription tier, paying per second of video streamed, paying a small tip to a creator. Sellers default to subscriptions, ad-supported content, or steep paywalls because the alternative would cost more to process than it collects.

### Solution

Stablecoin payments down to fractions of a cent settle directly between payer and seller, with no per-transaction fixed cost large enough to break the model. Pricing can match the unit of value (one article, one API call, one minute of stream, one model query), and a wallet can authorize small recurring or per-action payments without a card-network preauthorization flow in the middle.

### Why Ethereum

The fee floor on card payments exists because every transaction is intermediated by networks, processors, and banks that each take a fixed-cost slice. Settling small payments onchain removes that stack, so the unit of pricing can be the unit of value rather than what the rails can profitably process.

---

## Researcher credentials and peer review markets

ID: `peer-review-markets`
Domains: Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/peer-review-markets

### Problem

Academic recognition systems only reward first-author publications, leaving researchers who generate datasets, perform reviews, or replicate studies with no formal credit for work that is essential to science. Peer reviewers perform skilled labor for free on behalf of journals that charge institutions thousands per year — with reviews disappearing after use and no portable track record that follows the reviewer across journals.

### Solution

A market for peer review where journals post requests, qualified reviewers bid and are paid automatically on acceptance, and completed reviews become part of a portable verifiable track record — combined with credentials for dataset generation, replication work, and other non-publication contributions that carry the same weight as authorship.

### Why Ethereum

When each journal keeps its own record of who reviewed what, a reviewer's track record is scattered across publishers who have no reason to share it, and the labor stays invisible the moment they move on. Putting review and contribution history onchain keeps that record with the researcher, readable by any institution, rather than locked inside the publishers that benefit from the free work.

## Peer-to-peer energy markets

ID: `peer-to-peer-energy-markets`
Domains: Utilities
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/peer-to-peer-energy-markets

### Problem

Rooftop solar owners and other distributed generators have no direct way to sell surplus electricity to their neighbors, forced instead to feed it back to the grid at wholesale rates set by monopoly utilities.

### Solution

Local energy trading and microgrids that let participants buy, sell, and balance electricity directly with one another

### Why Ethereum

A monopoly utility sets the rate at which it buys back surplus solar and is the only party that can match neighbors who want to trade, so it has every reason to keep prices low and the market closed. Running local energy trading onchain lets neighbors transact directly on terms they agree to, with settlement that does not depend on the utility choosing to allow it.

## Drug authentication and supply chain traceability

ID: `pharmaceutical-traceability`
Domains: Health, Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/pharmaceutical-traceability

### Problem

A patient buying antimalarials has no way to verify the drug isn't one of the estimated 1-in-10 medicines in low-income markets that are substandard or falsified — counterfeit drugs with no active ingredient or toxic substitutes kill hundreds of thousands annually. The root cause is that pharmaceutical supply chains lack end-to-end verification from manufacturer to point of dispensing, making it impossible to confirm an unbroken chain of custody at the moment of sale.

### Solution

Per-unit identifiers linked to an onchain record of each drug's journey from manufacturer to shelf — allowing any pharmacist or patient with a smartphone to verify authenticity at the point of dispensing, while giving regulators end-to-end supply chain visibility to detect where counterfeits enter.

### Why Ethereum

A traceability system owned by one manufacturer or distributor can be edited to hide where counterfeits entered, and a pharmacist or patient has no way to check a record the same company controls. Recording each custody transfer onchain keeps the chain back to the manufacturer verifiable by anyone with a scan, so fraudulent insertion cannot be quietly written out.

## Physical goods marketplaces

ID: `physical-goods-marketplaces`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/physical-goods-marketplaces

### Problem

Peer-to-peer resale of physical goods suffers from rampant fraud because there is no trustworthy way to verify item authenticity or enforce payment-on-delivery without a costly intermediary.

### Solution

Tokenized listings and escrowed settlement bring transparency to resale and secondary markets

### Why Ethereum

A marketplace platform holds the funds, decides every dispute, and can favor whichever side it prefers or take fees for the privilege of being trusted. Holding payment in escrow onchain lets buyer and seller transact without trusting each other or a company, with release bound to confirmed delivery rather than a platform's judgment.

## Player-owned in-game assets

ID: `player-owned-in-game-assets`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/player-owned-in-game-assets

### Problem

In-game items, currencies, and progress are locked inside proprietary platforms that can freeze accounts, change economies, or shut down entirely, leaving players with no real ownership of assets they earned or purchased.

### Solution

Truly portable items/currency with minimal fees, rentals, AMM-driven markets, escrowed prize pools—shifting power from platforms to players

### Why Ethereum

When items and currency live on a studio's servers, the operator can freeze accounts, rewrite the economy, or shut the game down, and players keep nothing they earned. Holding assets onchain keeps ownership with the player and lets items move to any game or marketplace that supports the standard, beyond the reach of a single operator's kill switch.

## Portable credentials and professional identity

ID: `portable-professional-credentials`
Domains: Identity
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/portable-professional-credentials

### Problem

Academic credentials are issued as PDFs locked in institutional databases, skills acquired across employers and platforms exist in disconnected silos, and workers lose their ratings and reputation every time they switch platforms. NGO workers and journalists face the same problem in higher-stakes form: they must repeatedly prove affiliations in hostile environments while sharing full identity documents puts them at risk of surveillance and retaliation.

### Solution

Tamper-proof, portable credentials — diplomas, micro-credentials, work history, ratings, union membership, press credentials — that workers and professionals own and carry across platforms, employers, and jurisdictions, with selective disclosure so only the relevant claim is disclosed in each context.

### Why Ethereum

When credentials live in an institution's database or a hiring platform's records, the worker depends on that operator to stay in business, stay cooperative, and not gate access behind its own terms. Issuing them onchain lets the holder carry proof of their qualifications themselves, disclose only the relevant claim, and have it checked by anyone without routing through a company that can revoke or surveil that access.
