## Portable ratings & reviews

ID: `portable-ratings-reviews`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/portable-ratings-reviews

### Problem

A review you write on one platform stays there. Your accumulated reputation as a reliable reviewer, the products you have actually purchased, and the ratings you have given are siloed by Amazon, Yelp, Google, and each marketplace, and cannot travel with you to a new app or be carried into a context where the host platform has not approved it. A buyer searching for trustworthy review history on a new platform faces a cold start: the reputational signal is thin or missing entirely.

### Solution

Ratings and reviews kept as portable attestations the reviewer signs and controls, with the underlying purchase or interaction proven by an onchain receipt or credential. A reviewer's history travels with them across marketplaces and apps, a buyer can check whether a reviewer actually bought what they reviewed, and a new platform can bootstrap on existing reputation rather than starting from zero.

### Why Ethereum

When reviews live inside each marketplace, the platform owns the reputational signal and the writer cannot move it elsewhere. Recording reviews and the receipts behind them onchain keeps both with the reviewer, so the same reputation can be presented on any app and a receipt cannot be silently dropped by a platform that finds it inconvenient.

---

## Portable social identity and reputation

ID: `portable-social-identity`
Domains: Identity
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/portable-social-identity

### Problem

Users who build audiences on one social platform lose everything if they switch apps or get de-platformed. Follower counts and engagement metrics are also easily manipulated and impossible to verify independently.

### Solution

Onchain handles, profiles, and social graphs that work across multiple apps — combined with verifiable attestations for engagement and community participation that users own and carry with them.

### Why Ethereum

On a conventional social platform the company owns the follower graph, so it can de-platform a creator or change the rules and the audience does not come along. Holding the handle and social graph onchain keeps the connection between a person and their audience with the people involved, readable by any app, and survivable if one platform turns hostile or disappears.

---

## Clinical trial pre-registration and results registry

ID: `pre-registration-and-results`
Domains: Science, Health
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/pre-registration-and-results

### Problem

Pharmaceutical companies register clinical trials, then selectively publish only the results that support their drug — a practice called outcome reporting bias that systematically distorts the medical evidence base and leads doctors to prescribe treatments that don't work or cause harm, because negative results simply disappear.

### Solution

A registry where trial protocols and primary endpoints are cryptographically committed before a trial begins — making it publicly provable whether published results match what was pre-registered and impossible to quietly bury unfavorable outcomes.

### Why Ethereum

A registry run by an industry body or a single institution can quietly let sponsors amend protocols or delay results, since the same parties that benefit from burying outcomes influence the registrar. Committing protocols onchain fixes the original record where no sponsor or operator can revise it, so anyone can check published results against what was promised.

---

## Procurement

ID: `procurement`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/procurement

### Problem

Purchase orders, vendor agreements, and replenishment workflows run through email chains and disconnected ERP modules, with each party keeping its own copy of every transaction. Disputes over terms that were never machine-readable cause delays and duplicate orders. At month-end the same economic event lives as two separate records that have to be manually reconciled, consuming a large share of close-cycle time, and audit preparation depends on weeks of counterparty-confirmation letters.

### Solution

Purchase orders, vendor agreements, and replenishment schedules recorded as smart contracts that both buyer and vendor confirm at the point of origination. The same record serves both sides' books, so neither can later claim a different version, routine reorders trigger without manual sign-off, and the reconciliation step at close disappears because the record was joint from the start.

### Why Ethereum

When procurement and intercompany accounting run through one company's ERP, the terms and the transactions are only as reliable as that party's records, and either side can later claim a different version. Putting the agreement and the transaction record onchain gives both parties the same machine-readable history that neither can revise alone, so the workflow and the audit trail do not depend on trusting one counterparty's system.

---

## Public procurement lifecycle

ID: `public-procurement-lifecycle`
Domains: Government
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/public-procurement-lifecycle

### Problem

Government procurement processes are rife with opaque bid evaluations, paper-based contract trails, and limited public visibility, creating fertile ground for favoritism and corruption.

### Solution

Transparent record of tenders, bids, evaluations, awards, supplier credentials, deliveries, and payments spanning the full procurement cycle to reduce corruption and enable public audit

### Why Ethereum

When the procurement record is held by the same agency awarding the contracts, the office with the most to gain from favoritism is also the one that controls what the public gets to see. Recording the full lifecycle onchain keeps bids, evaluations, and payments outside that agency's editing power, so citizens and auditors can check the process without asking permission.

---

## Referral and affiliate payouts

ID: `referral-affiliate-payouts`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/referral-affiliate-payouts

### Problem

Referral and affiliate programs run inside the company's own systems. It tracks who referred whom, decides which conversions count, and controls the payout schedule. Referrers have to trust that attribution, disputes over whether a referral was credited are routine, and multi-step affiliate chains are hard for anyone outside the company to audit.

### Solution

Referral attribution and payout rules encoded so that a qualifying conversion, a signup or a purchase that meets the agreed terms, settles the payout to the referrer on its own. The referrer can confirm their referrals were counted and read the payout rules directly, and a chain of affiliates can each be paid from the same event without the company reconciling every tier by hand.

### Why Ethereum

A referral program has the company paying people it has a standing incentive to underpay, while also being the only party that records who referred what. Putting attribution and payout rules onchain lets referrers verify their own conversions against rules they can read, so the program does not rest on trusting the dashboard of the business writing the checks.

## Regenerative practice incentives

ID: `regenerative-practice-incentives`
Domains: Food & Agriculture, Environment
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/regenerative-practice-incentives

### Problem

Farmers who adopt soil-building, biodiversity-enhancing, or low-input practices absorb higher costs and risks with no reliable mechanism to measure, certify, and compensate them for the ecological value they create.

### Solution

Reward mechanisms that compensate farmers for sustainable and regenerative agricultural behaviors

### Why Ethereum

When a single program operator records which practices were adopted and decides who gets paid, farmers depend on that intermediary's bookkeeping and funders cannot tell whether the money reached genuine impact. Recording adoption and outcomes onchain creates a payment trail that funders can verify directly and that no intermediary can revise to favor itself.

## Reinsurance

ID: `reinsurance`
Domains: Insurance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/reinsurance

### Problem

Reinsurance capital is locked behind opaque, relationship-driven markets accessible only to large institutional players, with high intermediation costs and no way for cedents or investors to independently audit counterparty exposure or track payout obligations in real time.

### Solution

A reinsurance protocol where cedents and capital providers transact directly. Risk tranches are tokenized, payouts settle automatically when a loss event is verified, and reserve levels and counterparty exposure update onchain as positions change. Any participant can audit positions and obligations in real time, rather than waiting on quarterly disclosures and rating-agency snapshots.

### Why Ethereum

Reinsurance today is intermediated through a small set of brokers, and a cedent's view of a counterparty's book comes from quarterly financials and ratings rather than the live state of its positions. Settling it onchain keeps reserve levels and obligations verifiable by every participant in real time, and lowers the access threshold for new capital providers and smaller cedents to take part.

## Renewable project financing

ID: `renewable-project-financing`
Domains: Finance, Environment, Utilities
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/renewable-project-financing

### Problem

Small-scale renewable energy projects struggle to attract financing because ownership, cash flows, and performance data are not standardized or auditable, making it prohibitively hard to bundle many sites into investable instruments.

### Solution

Onchain funding models for solar, storage, and community energy projects that track ownership, cash flows, and performance

### Why Ethereum

When a financing platform holds the ownership records and reports the performance data, investors depend on that operator's books and it can favor its own deals or fold and strand the projects. Recording ownership, cash flows, and generation data onchain keeps them auditable by anyone, so small projects can be bundled and financed without trusting a single intermediary's accounting.

## Residential leasing

ID: `residential-leasing`
Domains: Real Estate & Housing
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/residential-leasing

### Problem

Lease management involves manual rent collection, opaque deposit handling, and paper-based renewals that create disputes between landlords and tenants with no neutral enforcement mechanism.

### Solution

Lease payments, deposits, renewals and dispute resolution run as smart contracts, eliminating many intermediaries

### Why Ethereum

In a normal lease the landlord holds the deposit and controls the paperwork, so a tenant depends on that landlord's goodwill to get terms honored and money returned. Running rent, deposits, and renewals onchain fixes the terms in a smart contract both parties agreed to and can inspect, so neither side can quietly change them and disputes resolve against a record no one owns alone.

## Revenue bonds

ID: `revenue-bonds`
Domains: Business Operations
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/revenue-bonds

### Problem

Revenue-based financing lets a business raise capital and repay investors a set percentage of revenue until a return cap, instead of taking on fixed debt or giving up equity. Repayment depends on the business reporting revenue honestly and routing the payments on schedule, so investors fund against numbers they cannot see directly. Enforcement comes down to an audit clause or a lawsuit, which prices small issuers and small investors out of the instrument.

### Solution

A revenue-share bond where incoming revenue passes through a contract that routes the agreed percentage to bondholders as it arrives and stops once the return cap is reached. Repayment is a property of the revenue flow rather than something the issuer has to remember to do or investors have to chase, and the outstanding balance is visible to both sides at every point.

### Why Ethereum

When the issuer controls the books and the bank account, investors in a revenue-share deal depend on self-reported revenue and the issuer's willingness to remit on time. Settling the split onchain makes the repayment rule and the full payment history something both sides verify directly, so a small business can raise this way without investors needing to fund an audit to check the accounting.

---

## Prediction markets for scientific claims

ID: `scientific-claim-markets`
Domains: Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/scientific-claim-markets

### Problem

Research funding committees allocate billions based on grant applications reviewed by small expert panels, with no mechanism to aggregate what the broader scientific community actually believes about which hypotheses are likely to replicate, which drugs will fail trials, or which research directions will prove fruitful — leaving funding systematically biased toward incremental work from established labs.

### Solution

Prediction markets where researchers stake tokens on the outcomes of specific scientific claims — will this trial replicate, will this drug hit its primary endpoint — with payouts flowing to those who were right. Market prices surface collective scientific belief in real time, and accumulated winnings serve as a credibility signal for funding allocation.

### Why Ethereum

A prediction market run by one company depends on that operator to hold the stakes, settle honestly, and not exclude participants or views it dislikes, and it can shut the market down when results embarrass powerful funders. Running it onchain keeps the stakes, the settlement rules, and the track record outside any single operator's control and auditable by anyone weighing the signal.

---

## Scientific knowledge graph

ID: `scientific-knowledge-graph`
Domains: Science
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/scientific-knowledge-graph

### Problem

Scientific knowledge is scattered across millions of papers and databases with no common layer connecting a finding to the data behind it, the studies that replicated or failed to replicate it, or the retractions that revised it. Whether a given result still stands is hard to see, and cross-domain connections are found mostly by accident.

### Solution

An onchain knowledge graph that links papers to their underlying data, their replications, and their retractions, maintained as a public resource rather than inside one publisher's database. A researcher or an application can trace a finding's current standing and follow connections across disciplines without negotiating access.

### Why Ethereum

A knowledge graph owned by one publisher or database vendor would let that operator decide which findings connect, who can build on the layer, and what gets charged for access, recreating the silos the project is trying to dissolve. Building it onchain keeps the connective layer outside any single institution's control, so any researcher or application can link findings across disciplines without negotiating for permission.

---

## Sourcing records for small-scale producers

ID: `small-producer-sourcing`
Domains: Food & Agriculture, Logistics & Trade
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/small-producer-sourcing

### Problem

A coffee cooperative in Guatemala that practices organic farming can't access premium export markets because the cost of formal certification (USDA Organic, Rainforest Alliance) is $5,000–15,000 per year — prohibitive for producers grossing $50,000. Without certification, buyers have no way to verify claims about growing practices, and the cooperative's product is priced as commodity-grade regardless of actual quality.

### Solution

Lightweight, verifiable sourcing records that document growing practices, input usage, and post-harvest handling at the cooperative level — creating a provenance trail that export buyers and roasters can verify without requiring expensive third-party certification as the only trust signal.

### Why Ethereum

When the only accepted proof of farming practices is a certification body charging fees a small cooperative cannot afford, that body becomes a gatekeeper deciding who reaches premium markets. Recording sourcing claims onchain lets a cooperative build provenance that buyers verify directly, so a track record accrues to the producer rather than to a certifier's private files.

## Sovereign & municipal bonds

ID: `sovereign-municipal-bonds`
Domains: Government, Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/sovereign-municipal-bonds

### Problem

Issuing and settling government debt involves layers of intermediaries, T+2 or longer settlement windows, and high minimum denominations that exclude smaller investors from participating.

### Solution

Onchain issuance, settlement, and coupon tracking of public debt instruments, enabling faster settlement, lower costs, and broader investor access

### Why Ethereum

The intermediaries that clear and custody government debt set the minimum sizes, the settlement timelines, and the fees, and they decide which investors get access at all. Issuing bonds onchain lets coupons and settlement run on public rules, so smaller investors can hold debt directly and the terms are not gated by the firms that profit from the layers in between.

---

## Spot freight market for trucking

ID: `spot-freight-trucking`
Domains: Logistics & Trade, Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/spot-freight-trucking

### Problem

Freight brokers sit between shippers who need loads moved and carriers who have trucks available, taking 15–20% margins on every transaction in exchange for making the match — a spread that exists almost entirely because the broker holds the relationship and information asymmetry, not because they add logistical value that a transparent protocol couldn't replace.

### Solution

A spot freight marketplace where shippers post loads with specifications and payment terms, carriers bid directly, payment is escrowed onchain and released automatically upon verified delivery, and both parties build a public reputation from their transaction history — cutting out the broker layer on transactions that don't require physical coordination.

### Why Ethereum

A freight marketplace run by one company recreates the broker problem: the operator holds the relationships and the reputation data, sets the take rate, and can drop a shipper or carrier from the market it controls. Running the marketplace onchain keeps the escrow and the reputation history outside any one operator's hands, so carriers carry their record between platforms and neither side depends on a middleman to hold funds honestly.

## Title & escrow

ID: `title-escrow`
Domains: Real Estate & Housing
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/title-escrow

### Problem

Real estate closings take 30-60 days and require title companies, notaries, and attorneys to manually verify ownership chains in paper registries, adding thousands of dollars in fees to every transaction.

### Solution

Smart contracts replace paper registries and manual escrow flows, reducing settlement time and improving transparency

### Why Ethereum

Title companies and escrow agents sit between buyer and seller, hold the funds, and are the sole authority on whether ownership records are correct, which adds cost and a point of failure both parties must trust. Recording title and escrow onchain keeps the ownership chain auditable by anyone and releases funds against conditions neither side can quietly rewrite.

## Tokenized policies for resale

ID: `tokenized-policies-for-resale`
Domains: Insurance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/tokenized-policies-for-resale

### Problem

Insurance policies are illiquid, non-transferable instruments that policyholders cannot sell, swap, or restructure if their risk profile changes, trapping capital and limiting flexibility.

### Solution

Policies become tradable contracts, enabling secondary markets, swapping risk profiles and unlocking liquidity

### Why Ethereum

An insurer that keeps policies non-transferable benefits directly from the trapped capital, and a resale market it operates lets it decide who may sell and at what terms. Representing policies onchain moves the contract and its transfer rights out of the issuer's exclusive control, so a policyholder can sell or restructure coverage without the carrier's permission.

## Loyalty points as liquid, transferable assets

ID: `tradable-loyalty-points`
Domains: Commerce
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/tradable-loyalty-points

### Problem

Frequent flyers and hotel loyalty members collectively hold an estimated $500 billion in unredeemed points — but those points expire silently, can't be combined across programs, can't be sold, and can be devalued unilaterally by the issuing company overnight with no recourse for holders.

### Solution

Tokenized loyalty points that are transferable between programs, sellable on secondary markets, and governed by transparent, immutable issuance and expiry rules — so holders have real property rights over value they've earned.

### Why Ethereum

When points live in an issuer's private database, the company that owes the value also writes the rules, and it can devalue balances, block transfers, or expire points overnight with no recourse for holders. Issuing loyalty value onchain puts the balance and its issuance rules where the holder can see and move them, so earned value behaves like property rather than a revocable entry.

## Trade credit clearing

ID: `trade-credit-clearing`
Domains: Finance
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/trade-credit-clearing

### Problem

SMEs extend trade credit to each other in isolated bilateral relationships, missing opportunities to net circular obligations and free up working capital that is locked in receivables chains.

### Solution

Netting obligations across SME networks

### Why Ethereum

A clearing operator that sees every firm's receivables holds a detailed map of who owes whom, and it can prioritize certain members, set the fees, or exclude competitors from the netting. Running the obligations onchain keeps the record out of any single firm's hands, so SMEs can net circular debt without handing a private intermediary leverage over their cash flow.

## Creator royalties for game mods and user content

ID: `ugc-mod-royalties`
Domains: Media
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/ugc-mod-royalties

### Problem

Modders and content creators build maps, skins, and tools that drive player engagement, but receive no automatic compensation because platforms lack enforceable revenue-sharing mechanisms tied to actual usage.

### Solution

Tokenized blueprints, maps or mods permit automatic revenue splits, cross-client recognition, and creator-driven extension of game logic

### Why Ethereum

When a game platform decides whether and how modders get paid, the company that profits from their work also sets the payout rules and can change or withhold them at will. Putting the royalty logic onchain ties creator splits to actual usage in a way no single platform controls, so compensation does not depend on a publisher choosing to honor it.

## Water rights trading and usage verification

ID: `water-rights-markets`
Domains: Utilities, Environment
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/water-rights-markets

### Problem

In drought-prone regions, water rights are traded in informal bilateral markets with no price transparency, while actual usage is monitored by infrequent physical inspections that miss illegal diversions — creating a tragedy of the commons where overuse is profitable and nearly undetectable until aquifers are depleted.

### Solution

Tokenized water rights tradeable on transparent markets, with IoT-verified usage continuously recorded onchain — creating a real-time allocation registry where overuse is immediately visible and rights can be transferred without paper title processes.

### Why Ethereum

If one agency or company runs the allocation registry, large water users can pressure it to overlook diversions or keep trades quiet, leaving downstream users with no independent view. Recording allocations and metered usage onchain lets every rights holder see the same picture, so overuse is visible to the people it harms.

## Wearables and health data exchanges

ID: `wearables-and-health-data-exchanges`
Domains: Health, AI
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/wearables-and-health-data-exchanges

### Problem

Wearable devices generate valuable biometric data that is locked inside proprietary platforms, giving individuals no way to share, monetize, or direct their own fitness and health information to researchers or insurers on their own terms.

### Solution

A standard for wearable biometric data, such as continuous glucose readings, sleep stages, or heart-rate variability, where the individual holds custody and grants time-bounded access to specific buyers. Each reading is signed at the device, so a researcher or insurer can trust it has not been altered after capture. Payment for access settles to the individual rather than to the wearable platform, and access ends automatically when the agreed window or condition closes.

### Why Ethereum

When biometric data sits inside a wearable company's platform, that company decides who buys it and keeps the value while the individual carries the breach risk. Giving people custody of their own health data onchain lets them direct it to a researcher or insurer on their own terms and capture what it is worth.

## Whistleblower & evidence integrity

ID: `whistleblower-evidence-integrity`
Domains: Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/whistleblower-evidence-integrity

### Problem

Whistleblower testimonies and leaked evidence are vulnerable to tampering, metadata stripping, and retroactive denial, while existing submission channels routinely expose the identity of sources.

### Solution

Timestamping and storage of testimonies, photographs, or datasets with privacy-preserving disclosure

### Why Ethereum

A whistleblower submission channel run by any single organization can be subpoenaed, breached, or pressured into exposing who sent what, and the same operator could quietly alter or lose the evidence. Recording timestamped, privacy-preserving submissions onchain means the source does not have to trust an intermediary that can be compelled against them.

## Wills and estate execution

ID: `wills-estate-execution`
Domains: Civil Society
URL: https://usecaselab.org/idea/wills-estate-execution

### Problem

Estate execution depends on manual probate processes that take months or years, while trust administration requires fiduciaries to manually manage distributions and reporting across jurisdictions, with beneficiaries having limited visibility.

### Solution

Time-locked, oracle-triggered estate execution and programmable trust administration with transparent record-keeping — assets transfer automatically when verifiable conditions are met.

### Why Ethereum

When estate execution runs through a court, a bank, or a single executor, the people who hold the assets also decide when and whether to release them, and a beneficiary has little recourse against delay or self-dealing. Building the trust logic onchain keeps the release conditions and the record visible to every heir, so distribution follows rules nobody can quietly rewrite.
